Observe's session **detail** (not the list) carries `threads`: open cards
on that session that already have a message. The Firstmate session lists
Firstmate-authored cards; a crewmate session lists that task's. Empty
threads stay off the pane. `CardService.observeThreads` is the source;
the frame paints one header line per thread
(`[data-observe-threads]`, `"Title: N · last who"`). Observe remains
dev-only (`docs/dev-observe.md`).

"merge it", "land it", "discard it" typed under a crewmate's card is not the
crewmate's to run, and **nothing in the host reads those words**. The
crewmate's own instruction does the routing: it closes its card and carries
the captain's words verbatim into its `report`, which the whose-turn rule
routes to the Firstmate - the turn that then runs the settle it would have
run had he typed the same words in the main input.

That is the captain's Q2 as he corrected it: "crewmate should not answer the
user with 'not mine'. it should just close the card and pass the decision to
firstmate to execute."

It is never woken for a thread message (the captain's C9 A). Two bounded
facts reach it on whatever turn comes next:

The whose-turn rule gains one fact (`reportSort.ts`): an unanswered captain
message in a thread is the CREWMATE's turn, so its report wakes nobody. It
is branch 0, above the open-card branch, deliberately - the captain has
spoken since that card went up, so the card no longer holds the turn.

The design skill owns every visual rule

# The task record and its protocol

The task as a record (task-system P0) and the wire protocol over it (P3). `docs/architecture.md` §19 summarizes the whole task system; capture is `docs/task-capture.md`, the graph `docs/task-graph.md`, retention `docs/task-retention.md`.

## The idle clock

Four columns on the record (migration 45; new databases receive them with
the record) hold the idle ladder's durable state, written only through
`TaskService` like every other column: `idle_since` (`markIdle` at every
idle boundary, `endIdle` when a turn the ladder did not start begins),
`recovery_rung`, `recovery_count` and `recovery_at` (`recordRecovery`).
They are machinery, not a state change: no timeline event and no
`updated_at`. What reads them is `CrewSupervisor.reconcileIdle` and the
crew line's `stalled` fact (`docs/report-sort.md`, "The idle ladder").

## Derived, never stored: the basis and the review join

The record keeps no stamp of a fact the graph already holds (migration 46
removed the two it had). A task's `basis` is stored on its shape as the
Firstmate named it (a key or an id); whether it holds - the named task is
done or has reported - is derived at every read (`TaskService.basisHolds`,
`basisOf`), so a step planned behind a still-running task reads grounded
the moment that task answers, with no write. The store strips
`basis_verified` from any shape it is handed; the router still receives it,
derived, beside the shape. The basis reads the same everywhere it is shown:
`tasks.detail` carries `basis: { ref, verified }`, `v_tasks_v1` a `basis`
column, and the export the shape verbatim. A review's builder is its parent
(the one stored join), and which review a builder's verdict came from is
read off that edge (`TaskService.verdictReviewOf`: the newest review child
opened at or before `reviewedAt`), never cached in the builder's delivery
facts; the verdict's timeline event still names the review in its data,

- the close rule at `piResources.ts:92`;
- `close_card` on the captain's behalf - only a card's own author withdraws
  it now, and the captain's × is the only dismissal (`CardService.close`
  refuses a Firstmate close of anyone else's card and names the door);
- the Jev pre-step and the relay classifier, which were the alternatives
  this design replaced. Neither was ever built.

## The record

`card_messages` (migration 38): card id, who (`captain | crewmate |
firstmate | host`), text, at. `CardStore` owns it beside `card_revisions`,
and a thread dies with its card - `deleteForTask` removes both in one
transaction, so the D-13 purge and a task's own close need no new rule.

`CardService.addMessage` is the single writer: the captain's reply,
an author's prose answer and the host's own "revised" line all go through
it, so nothing writes a thread row without the `fm:cards:thread` push that
paints it.

A captain reply on a crewmate's card is a captain STEER to that crewmate -
the same control-plane path a card click takes - stamped `via: "thread"`
(`steerViaSchema`) with the card's id, carrying `THREAD_STEER_PREAMBLE` and
then his words verbatim. Delivery is not awaited, exactly as a card click's
round-trip is not: the message is on the record the moment it is typed, and
a delivery failure is a feed line rather than a lost reply.

A reply resolves nothing. The buttons stay pinned, and a card still leaves
the stage on a button, a settle, the captain's close, the author's
withdrawal, or a note's seen-collapse - all host code.

A reply does hand the turn to the author, and the shell shows it: the card
leaves the stage until the author has answered and closed out - see the
next section. A refused reply restores it with the draft kept.

## When a card reaches the stage

Captain-approved on a board in two rounds on 2026-09-27 ("ship it",
verdict "Ship it as recommended"; the decided design is sections 0, 6 and
R2 of `fm3000-card-return-closeout-r1/design-excerpt.md`). It replaced the
renderer's own hide, which brought a card back on its author's FIRST write
after the reply, whatever it said: 10 of 25 answered replies on the
captain's install came back before the answer was settled - 4
acknowledgements ("I'll assess..."), 4 author addenda seconds apart, 2
corrections after a Firstmate steer.

**One rule for every crewmate card** (the captain's Q1 A and Q5 A): a
crewmate's card - new, revised, or answered in its thread - reaches the
stage at the crewmate's CLOSE-OUT after its last write: its next `report`,
or its idle (its resumable turn ending), whichever comes first. Cancellation
and terminal session failure close the task and retire all its open cards,
including hidden replies, Working cards and pending revisions, without
releasing them onto the stage. Card rows, revisions and threads remain on
the record; they do not return after restart. A recoverable provider-failed
turn or interruption is still an idle boundary, not a task close. Emission
also rechecks the task at publication, so a completion check that finishes
after closure cannot recreate a retired choice. A
captain reply takes the card off the stage, and it stays off while his line
is the newest on the thread. Every write in between lands on the record and
paints the thread; the stage does not move. A card already on the stage
that its crewmate revises keeps showing what it showed - a keeps-open
click's Working chip included - and redraws in place at the close-out.

**The Firstmate's own cards** keep working as they did (the captain's Q3
A): they go up and redraw at once, its turn's end is its close-out, and
its closing words are its thread answer - for the reply its turn was about
and, since contract v4.14, for one it read mid-turn - unless it revised the
card. When the answer needs a crewmate, its persona says to say so in the
card and revise the same card when the answer lands, never to answer a
thread with a new card.

**The hidden state lives in the core** (the captain's Q4 A): `Card.awaiting`
on the card snapshot - `answer` while the captain's line is the newest on
the thread, `close-out` while the author has written and not yet closed out,
absent on a card the stage shows. `CardService` is its one writer: the
captain's line sets `answer` (`addMessage`), any later line ends it (the
author's answer, or the host's `revised:` for a revision), every crewmate
write holds a new or hidden card for its close-out, and `closeOut` - called
from the crewmate's `report` and its resumable turn's end, and the
Firstmate's turn end - releases what waited on that author. `snapshot()` is
the stage: a card on it whose author has written again is pushed as the
version the stage showed until the close-out. The column is `cards.awaiting`
(migration 52), so a hide survives a restart and a reload; the restart is
itself every author's close-out, so a card that only waited on one reaches
the stage at boot. A click resolves against the version on the stage.

What reads it: the renderer shows a card only when it is not awaiting
(`visibleCards`) and has no door of its own - a thread message never brings
a card back, and a card's return is an arrival: onto the stage when nothing
else is shown, else behind the shown card, unread, with the notice pulse.
`sendReply` takes the card off the stage at once, as the core's push then
confirms. The native notifier counts a card only once it is on the stage,
so a return notifies like an arrival. Observe and the tests read the same
snapshot.

What does not read it: the whose-turn rule and the idle ladder read the
record, where the card is open from its emit and the captain's line is a
thread fact, exactly as before (R2: "only the stage waits").

**While the author works**: nothing on the stage, and one feed line at
reply time on a crewmate's card - `You asked crewmate N under "<title>"`
through `broadcastEvent` (the captain's Q2 A); a Firstmate card's reply
already has its "Captain: ..." line. The card's return is its own notice.
The task timeline records each crewmate card's stage moment as its
`card_raised` event, written at the close-out with the close-out that
released it (`data.closeOut`: `report`, `idle`, `restart`), and again on a
return after the captain's reply (`data.returned`), so the replay can count
a late return.

**The contract** (v4.14): the crewmate's thread steer preamble and
`CARD_REPLY` say to do the work his words need first, answer once - revise
the card, or reply when nothing on it changes - then report, because the
card comes back when you are done; never acknowledge or announce.

## The contract both agents read

`CARD_REPLY` in `src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts` is ONE text, included
exactly once by every persona beside `CARD_AUTHORING` (the captain's Q4 B:
"this is not just crewmate - firstmate should largely share the same
contract"). It says: revise the card when the reply changes what the card
should say (same id, `emit_card`); answer in prose when nothing on the card
changes; a reply is prose only - no actions, no script, no figure; and a
reply resolves nothing. Since v4.14 it also says when: the work comes
first and the answer once, because the card comes back only when its
author is done. `piResources.test.ts` pins that every persona carries it
once and no tool description repeats a sentence of it, the same structural
pin `CARD_AUTHORING` has.

A crewmate gains one output for that answer: `reply(card_id, text)`
(`crewmateTaskTools.ts`, Claude twin in `claudeTaskTools.ts`), beside
`report` / `emit_card` / `note_progress` / `file_followup`. Its description
carries call mechanics only. The Firstmate's tool count is unchanged at 24
- there is no Firstmate `reply` tool; it answers the same two ways through
`emit_card` and its closing words.

## Firstmate-card threads (phase 2)

A captain reply on the Firstmate's own card is a captain TURN about that
card, not a steer. `cardTakesReplies` is true for a Firstmate author;
`CrewSupervisor.replyToCard` files the captain's message and calls
`converseAboutCard` (`FirstmateAgent.converse` with `aboutCardId`). The
about line replaces the maybe-hint:

`about: card <id> (<presentation>) "<title>" - the captain replied in its thread`

The Firstmate answers through the same `CARD_REPLY` shape: revise the card
under the same id (the host's "revised:" line already records that) or
leave closing words as prose (`recordFirstmateThreadAnswer`, only when the
newest thread message is still the captain's). A parked idle turn keeps the
card on its inbox ref (`captain-turn:card:<id>`); a mid-turn reply rides
the existing steer with the about line in context, and since v4.14 the
turn's closing words answer it too, because the card now waits for an
answer across restarts. Contract v4.2 is unchanged; the wire bump is
protocol 1.19.0 for images on `fm:cards:reply`.

## Images on steers (phase 2)

Pi's `steer(text, images)` already existed. The Claude Agent SDK accepts
the same bytes as user-message image blocks
(`{ type: "image", source: { type: "base64", media_type, data } }`) on
both `prompt` and `steer`. The durable inbox stores text only, so a
copy that cannot keep the bytes says so with that note instead of dropping
them silently; a live native session carries the bytes on the call.

`fm:cards:reply` takes the same union converse does (words, or
`{ text?, images? }`). An image-only reply is stored as `"sent a picture"`.
The reply row pastes pictures the way the main input does. Its field is the
composer's own (`ComposerField`, `docs/composer.md` "The card reply row"):
the same keys, growth to 5 lines, and the count and refusal against
`CARD_REPLY_MAX_CHARS`. Thread messages keep their line breaks.

Observe's session **detail** (not the list) carries `threads`: open cards
on that session that already have a message. The Firstmate session lists
Firstmate-authored cards; a crewmate session lists that task's. Empty
threads stay off the pane. `CardService.observeThreads` is the source;
the frame paints one header line per thread
(`[data-observe-threads]`, `"Title: N · last who"`). Observe remains
dev-only (`docs/dev-observe.md`).

## The settle hand-off, with no classifier

"merge it", "land it", "discard it" typed under a crewmate's card is not the
crewmate's to run, and **nothing in the host reads those words**. The
crewmate's own instruction does the routing: it closes its card and carries
the captain's words verbatim into its `report`, which the whose-turn rule
routes to the Firstmate - the turn that then runs the settle it would have
run had he typed the same words in the main input.

That is the captain's Q2 as he corrected it: "crewmate should not answer the
user with 'not mine'. it should just close the card and pass the decision to
firstmate to execute."

## How the Firstmate learns

It is never woken for a thread message (the captain's C9 A). Two bounded
facts reach it on whatever turn comes next:

- **"thread activity since your last turn"** - a context-block section
  beside `renderCaptainResolutions`, one line per card: who wrote last, the
  first ~120 characters, how many messages, and whether the author still
  owes an answer. Bounded exactly like the resolutions (8 lines, 6 h), with
  the same watermark, so a busy conversation cannot swell the block.
- **`thread:` on the task's crew line** - `2 messages, last from captain`,
  from `CardService.threadFact`; `crew_status` carries the same field.

The whose-turn rule gains one fact (`reportSort.ts`): an unanswered captain
message in a thread is the CREWMATE's turn, so its report wakes nobody. It
is branch 0, above the open-card branch, deliberately - the captain has
spoken since that card went up, so the card no longer holds the turn.

## The shell

The design skill owns every visual rule
(`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/cards/CardThread.prompt.md`);
`src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx` implements it and
`threadGeometry.ts` holds the ladder's arithmetic.

While a card has no thread, "reply to this card…" is the very bottom of the
card, under the action row and one hairline above it (the captain's tweak
3). A card with no author to reach - the host's own agent-down set - has no
reply row at all.

The first sent message opens the thread beside the card in ONE container
(tweak 1): one surface, border, radius and shadow, a single `--line-2`
hairline between the columns, the pair centred as one object. Thread
`clamp(0.4 × stage, 288, 360)`, card `min(W, stage − 32 − thread)`, where W
is the card's own width - 560 for a regular card, more for a wide or full
one or one the captain dragged (`docs/card-authoring.md` "Card width").

When the pair would leave the card under 400px the docked panels FOLD (tweak
2): `html[data-rails-folded]` gives the rails' width back to the stage and a
4px edge tab at each folded side says the panels are one click away - the
click closes the thread, which returns them. Fold is not collapse: a
collapsed dock still holds its full `--rail-width`, so collapsing frees
nothing. The rails keep their panels while folded, which is why
`--rail-docked-*` (what they ask for) is a different variable from
`--occupied-rail-*` (what they take): reading the effective one would make
the ladder circular and the pair would oscillate.

In place is the last rung - a segmented control in the card's head swaps the
body for the message list - and needs a stage under 720px, which the app's
own 960px window minimum puts out of reach.

`threadGeometry.test.ts` is the binding evidence: the R3.1 table at 960 /
1200 / 1440 / 1728 with both docks, one dock and none, and
`card-threads.spec.ts` measures the real shell against it - folded at the
default 1200 (both docks occupied leave a 600px stage) and beside the docks

One sharp edge paid for there: `--rail-docked-left|right` are REGISTERED

unregistered custom property computes to its own token stream, so
`--rail-docked-left: var(--rail-width)` reads back through
`getComputedStyle` as the literal `max(300px, 20vw)` and parses as `NaN`;
the ladder then placed the pair as if nothing were docked and it sat under
the rail. `useShellLayout` also observes the STAGE's size, because a rail
docking or undocking is not a render of the card layer.

Task waiting follows the version the stage shows, not the durable head
(`docs/task-record.md`, "Ready waiting is a presentation projection"). New
crewmate cards still release at report or idle, whichever comes first; report

once. Acknowledgement or an unreleased revision does not bring it back. An
unanswered reply stays hidden across restart; restart releases close-out and

# The task record and its protocol

The task as a record (task-system P0) and the wire protocol over it (P3). `docs/architecture.md` §19 summarizes the whole task system; capture is `docs/task-capture.md`, the graph `docs/task-graph.md`, retention `docs/task-retention.md`.

## The idle clock

Four columns on the record (migration 45; new databases receive them with
the record) hold the idle ladder's durable state, written only through
`TaskService` like every other column: `idle_since` (`markIdle` at every
idle boundary, `endIdle` when a turn the ladder did not start begins),
`recovery_rung`, `recovery_count` and `recovery_at` (`recordRecovery`).
They are machinery, not a state change: no timeline event and no
`updated_at`. What reads them is `CrewSupervisor.reconcileIdle` and the
crew line's `stalled` fact (`docs/report-sort.md`, "The idle ladder").

## Derived, never stored: the basis and the review join

The record keeps no stamp of a fact the graph already holds (migration 46
removed the two it had). A task's `basis` is stored on its shape as the
Firstmate named it (a key or an id); whether it holds - the named task is
done or has reported - is derived at every read (`TaskService.basisHolds`,
`basisOf`), so a step planned behind a still-running task reads grounded
the moment that task answers, with no write. The store strips
`basis_verified` from any shape it is handed; the router still receives it,
derived, beside the shape. The basis reads the same everywhere it is shown:
`tasks.detail` carries `basis: { ref, verified }`, `v_tasks_v1` a `basis`
column, and the export the shape verbatim. A review's builder is its parent
(the one stored join), and which review a builder's verdict came from is
read off that edge (`TaskService.verdictReviewOf`: the newest review child
opened at or before `reviewedAt`), never cached in the builder's delivery
facts; the verdict's timeline event still names the review in its data,
which is what the replay scorer reads.

## Ready waiting is a presentation projection

Approved specification: FI3-275, direction A, reachable cards, split waiting
children. Cancellation and terminal session failure retire task cards at
closure through `SettleService.closeRecord` (FI3-270); the waiting projection
also independently excludes closed tasks. `waitingCardId` is the sole waiting
fact: the first unresolved shown ready decision associated with a live task,
with no `awaiting` and nonempty actions, in `CardService.snapshot()` order.
Direct associations and captain-gate references use that same test. A ready
card behind the foreground card still counts; navigation can focus it. A
hidden or Working sibling cannot mask another ready decision. Closed tasks
always have null. Count each task once, not cards or ancestors.

`flags.needsYou` and project `counts.needsYou` retain broader durable attention
(cards, captain holds and dead dependencies); they no longer label a task as
waiting. Ready waiting also implies attention. Project `counts.waitingOnYou`
is the derived live-task waiting count (protocol 1.39.0). No task status,
readiness column or dispatch permission is added. Losing a waiting signal
never releases a gate. The record keeps generic attention/hold guidance and
existing lifecycle controls when there is no ready choice; a blocker or
interruption may still lead while Show the card remains available.

CardService declares stack changes through `presentationChanged` at its
broadcast seam, including pending shown-version revisions, reply holds,
close-out, Working/ready, retirement and restoration. `TaskService` alone
advances `task_board.seq` for that invalidation, without changing task rows,
updated/idle/recovery clocks, timeline or feed. TaskProtocol delivers the
focusable card snapshot before its board snapshot or delta, explicitly, not
by relative timer delays. `tasks.detail` re-reads on either board carrier as
well as its own events; project readers refresh too.

The renderer immediately overlays local card availability on board/detail
and project waiting counts when it hides a reply, or restores a refused one.
The read executor retains raw data as its delta base; local presentation does
not change seq. Older snapshots/deltas do not restore a hidden shortcut; gaps
re-read. In-flight reply pushes stay hidden, and a reply receipt refreshes the
stack if a fast author returned before the receipt. Task navigation and Show
the card refresh the association before focusing it, falling back to the
record rather than forcing a hidden card forward.

Tasks separates a waiting child from an underway parent tree. Nonwaiting
parents/siblings keep their existing grouping, nesting, sorting and activity
dots; no parent context is duplicated or counted as a decision. The binding
interface regression is `src/core/tasks/readyWaiting.test.ts`, joined through
real CardService, TaskProtocol and the read executor; the isolated app journey
is the ready-waiting case in `tests/e2e/card-threads.spec.ts`.

The two pinned surfaces moved: `window.firstmate` gained `tasks` and `projects` (`phase0-guardrails.spec.ts`); the self-map's channel and event lists are read from the contract itself.

# Crew orbital formation

The home character uses the captain's approved multi-plane configuration when
more than six work tasks are active (working **or** idle). Up to six crew keep
the original single-ring geometry, glyph sizing, motion and status posture.
There is no new setting, label or permanent orbit guide in the product.

## Approved configuration

The captain approved shipping the card configuration and explicitly confirmed
these settings:

| Plane | Radius | Tilt from the sky plane | Travel | Relative speed | Period |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Inner | 164 px | 42° | Forward | 0.5× | 128 s |
| Middle | 210 px | 65° | Reverse | 3× | about 31 s |
| Outer | 256 px | 16° | Reverse | 1× | about 125 s |

These are the card's speed multipliers relative to **each plane's original
Keplerian period**, not three multipliers of the same period. The original
periods were `64 s × (radius / 164)^(3/2)`. Forward follows the existing ring's
travel; reverse changes orbital travel, not the crewmate's own spin. The
line-of-nodes orientations remain −0.42, +0.38 and −0.70 radians.

The paths are 3D circles with a shared center and distinct radii. The camera is
orthographic; position and depth derive from the same projection. Differently
inclined paths can cross **on screen** without intersecting in 3D. The chosen
unequal speed multipliers are stylized choreography, not circular orbits under
one shared gravity field. The original no-overlap observations in the historical
prototype do not apply to this more strongly inclined approved configuration.

## Lifecycle

`crewSignal.ts` constructs the one shared `CrewOrbit` in `adaptive` mode, and the
existing home view paints it. `orbitalPlanes.ts` is the single home of the approved
constants and projection. The explicit `ring` mode remains available for the
historical comparison and regression tests; `DEFAULT_ORBIT` is unchanged.

At seven crew the ring eases into the three planes. At six it eases back. There
is no instantaneous position jump at either threshold: geometry, radius and
angular slots follow the existing springs. A settled boot roster is placed on
its planes immediately, without re-emitting already active crewmates.
Reduced motion snaps the formation and lifecycle clips to their settled state.

The inner (default) plane fills to six crew first, then the middle to six,
then the outer to six. Beyond 18, all three are full, so overflow continues
on the least-populated plane (ties favor inner first): 24 crew are 8/8/8. On
entering the crowded formation, slots are evenly distributed within each plane. Arrivals take the widest vacant angular gap in the first plane below
capacity. When a member leaves, the oldest member of the next occupied plane
glides into the gap, cascading from outer to middle only if needed. No other
member changes plane or slot; fast threshold bounces do not reverse the move.
The member's plane projection follows a spring, like its existing angle and
radius; reduced motion settles it immediately. Formation changes may re-space
slots within a plane. Reports, steers, launch trails and Firstmate cues use the
same projected path as the member; home/away departures, failure nudges and
working/idle colors are retained.
Crowded glyphs use the approved roughly 25-pixel base; idle crew retain the slow
spin and cool light rather than moving beyond the outer canvas boundary.
The far/near canvases also draw members in depth order within each layer. At
the minimum window height the crowded formation scales uniformly to fit above
the activity line and input, preserving the angles and relative radii; the small
ring stays at its original scale. The fit remains responsive with reduced motion enabled.

## Active adversarial review cue

A host-commissioned review task identifies the builder through its fixed parent edge and its
`shape.kind = review`. The task board and `task_changed` stream carry that typed `reviewOf` id;
an ordinary child cannot trigger the cue. While the review task remains active (including an
idle reviewer awaiting a re-review), the builder's existing solid gets two glowing electrons
on crossed orbits, with ember trails and no drawn rings. The electrons disappear as soon as
the review closes or the builder departs. Restart seeds
the same relationship from the live board, and two reviews of one builder do not cancel each
other when one ends.

The electrons and their 39° ember trails use the working wire token, including in the light
theme. Their base path radii are 70% of the original: 36.4 × 17.5 px for a 30 px crewmate;
this scales with the glyph, not the crew's orbital planes. At 8× the prototype's base orbital
periods (5.4 and 6.2 seconds), both paths gently wander in tilt and radius and their timing
drifts smoothly. This is a visual metaphor, not a physics simulation. It changes **none** of the crewmate's spin, position, working/idle color,
solid, or lifecycle. The far halves paint behind its wires, the near halves in front; reduced
motion renders one settled, unmoving frame. Nothing new is drawn around the Firstmate.

`crewSignal.test.ts` checks the live review start/close, unrelated children, multiple reviews,
unchanged crewmate spin and position, and boot; `crew-review-electrons.spec.ts` checks actual
ember pixels only for a live review and captures the real home view in dark and light under
`artifacts/crew-review-electrons/`.

## Tier solids

Each crewmate's solid is the intelligence slot it is served on (captain's board
verdict, 2026-09-23; rules in the design skill's `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`):

| Slot | Solid | Corners | Wires |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| low | tetrahedron | 4 | 6 |
| medium | octahedron | 6 | 12 |
| high | icosahedron | 12 | 30 |
| premium | geodesic sphere (the icosahedron, each face split in four) | 42 | 120 |

Every solid is inscribed in the same sphere, so the glyph size, the ring, the
planes and every motion are unchanged; denser solids draw finer. The slot is
`TaskView.tier` - the newest routing decision's `served` slot (the asked slot on a
row routed before `served` was recorded) - and rides `task_changed` so a re-route
moves the solid live. A crewmate whose slot is unknown (it never routed) is the
tetrahedron, pixel-identical to the pre-tier crewmate. The flicker, the filament
tick and reduced motion apply to every solid's own wires; `crewmate.ts` owns the
geometry (`TIER_SOLIDS`).

## Verification

- `orbitalPlanes.test.ts`: exact inclinations and relative angular rates, measured
  travel of the rendered frames, unchanged small-crew frames, depth and radius,
  inner-first capacity/overflow, inward glides and regrowth at 6/12/18,
  stable survivors, both thresholds, packets/cues, reduced motion, and finite
  bounds through 96 crew (not a readability guarantee at that density).
- `tests/e2e/crew-planes.spec.ts`: the real storage → boot board → shared model →
  home canvases at 6, 12, 13, 19, 24 and 48 crew, checking painted assignments
  through the shared helper; actual task events cross 6 → 7 → 6 → 7 and an
  oldest member's departure brings the next member inward; animated pixels
  resume after reduced motion, whose pixels remain still.
- The pre-existing `orbit`, `crewSignal`, painter/cue and `crew-orbit.spec.ts`
  tests continue to exercise the original lifecycle and actual commissioning.

Before/after 12-crew app captures and the inward-glide/settled 11-crew captures
are in `artifacts/crew-fill/`. Other captures are in
`artifacts/crew-planes/product/`. The earlier
`docs/prototypes/crew-planes.html` remains an explicitly historical study, not the
approved product's tuning surface. No card-only slider or generated card bundle
is imported into the product.

## Notes moved from AGENTS.md

Moved verbatim from `AGENTS.md` on 2026-09-24; `AGENTS.md` keeps a one-line pointer to each.

- The crew orbit (captain-approved board verdict 2026-09-14, `fm-homes/mini-default/data/fm3000-crew-orbit-anim-proto-s1/`): `src/renderer/src/character/crew/` - `orbit.ts` is the DOM-free time-injected model (the original ring through six crew, then an eased three-plane formation in the home view; captain-approved settings live in `orbitalPlanes.ts` and `docs/crew-orbits.md`: inner 0.5× forward/42°, middle 3× reverse/65°, outer 1× reverse/16°; `DEFAULT_ORBIT` stays the small-crew reference), `crewmate.ts` the painter, `CrewOrbit.tsx` two canvases (far/near) around the Firstmate for occlusion, `cues.ts` the Firstmate-side send-off/receive envelopes (ride `emoteSignal.ts` like the notice, no machine state), `crewSignal.ts` the wiring: one shared model fed from `applyEvent` and seeded settled from the boot board (restart is not a spawn) - a renderer-only side channel, never store state. A crewmate is a `work` task while `active`; working = host-derived `workPosture.state` active (see Continuing-work posture below). Color is the captain's call and overrides the old "crew never heats" reading: a working crewmate heats cyan -> ember like the rig, idle stays dim cyan (`crewmateLight`), and working/idle must still read in motion and posture. The solid is the crewmate's served slot (captain's board verdict 2026-09-23, `fm-homes/mini-default/data/fm3000-crew-tier-visuals-proto-s1/report.md`; `docs/crew-orbits.md` "Tier solids"): tetrahedron low, octahedron medium, icosahedron high, geodesic sphere premium, one shared sphere, never a hue/label/size/motion; `TaskView.tier` (newest routing decision's `served`) rides the board and `task_changed`, and an unknown slot is the tetrahedron, pixel-identical to the pre-tier crewmate. Reduced motion goes through `reducedMotion.ts`. `tests/e2e/crew-orbit.spec.ts`, `crew-planes.spec.ts` and `crew-tiers.spec.ts` read the real canvases.

## Continuing-work posture

Tasks dots, home-view crew heat/spin, and the working/idle counts read one
host-derived `workPosture` from the task board and `task_changed` events.
It is presentation only: `activity`, turn control, the idle clock and the
supervision witness order are unchanged. The card-thread Working badge still
reads turn activity.

Active means a running turn, a live host/client job, watched checks, deliverable
guidance (including retry backoff or a captured captain reply), captured
settlement, or a finite automatic wait. A decision card does not cool a worker
while evidenced work continues. Host jobs remain active past their two-hour
inspection bound; that bound remains a supervision rule, not proof of exit.
An account cut-off or quota gate pauses queued delivery. A question with no
continuing work and a dependency with no continuation are idle. Paused/unknown
postures stay cool; the Tasks dot's tooltip carries the reason. Interrupted
turns retain the danger dot unless continuing work is known.

The host refreshes sequenced presentation changes after job membership,
inbox, card/thread, account cut-off and task events, with reconciliation on the
existing ticker. Boot derives the same answer; persisted job rows are history,
not live jobs. Claude's complete background list replaces membership on each
signal. Attachment/transport loss invalidates the previous membership. Until
the installed client supplies a valid list, absence of background work is
unknown (the current SDK emits no startup list). This does not change recovery
or assume every installed client supports that signal.

content.content:
# Cards as threads

Every card is the head of a thread between the captain and the card's
AUTHOR. What he types under a card goes to that author, and the author
answers either by REVISING the card (preferred - the head re-renders and the
thread shows one host line) or with a prose message in the thread.

Captain-approved on the Lavish board on 2026-09-20 ("cards-as-threads over a
decision model - ship it"); the decided design is section R4 of
`fm3000-card-close-decision-model-s1/report.md`, R1-R3 carry the review
rounds in his own words, and `board/thread-prototype.html` is the shell
prototype he reviewed. This file is the one home for the feature as built
(phase 1 and phase 2).

## What it replaced

Before this, a captain message that addressed a card's content was a
Firstmate turn: a standing rule told the Firstmate to `close_card` first
that turn, whoever had emitted it, and then to relay his words to the
crewmate by hand. Over the five days the rule ran on the captain's own
install that was 61 close turns and 27 pure relays, each a flagship
inference at a median 9 s, and the record said the CAPTAIN had closed cards
he never touched.

Three things retire with it (the captain's Q3 A):

- the close rule at `piResources.ts:92`;
- `close_card` on the captain's behalf - only a card's own author withdraws
  it now, and the captain's × is the only dismissal (`CardService.close`
  refuses a Firstmate close of anyone else's card and names the door);
- the Jev pre-step and the relay classifier, which were the alternatives
  this design replaced. Neither was ever built.

## The record

`card_messages` (migration 38): card id, who (`captain | crewmate |
firstmate | host`), text, at. `CardStore` owns it beside `card_revisions`,
and a thread dies with its card - `deleteForTask` removes both in one
transaction, so the D-13 purge and a task's own close need no new rule.

`CardService.addMessage` is the single writer: the captain's reply,
an author's prose answer and the host's own "revised" line all go through
it, so nothing writes a thread row without the `fm:cards:thread` push that
paints it.

A captain reply on a crewmate's card is a captain STEER to that crewmate -
the same control-plane path a card click takes - stamped `via: "thread"`
(`steerViaSchema`) with the card's id, carrying `THREAD_STEER_PREAMBLE` and
then his words verbatim. Delivery is not awaited, exactly as a card click's
round-trip is not: the message is on the record the moment it is typed, and
a delivery failure is a feed line rather than a lost reply.

A reply resolves nothing. The buttons stay pinned, and a card still leaves
the stage on a button, a settle, the captain's close, the author's
withdrawal, or a note's seen-collapse - all host code.

A reply does hand the turn to the author, and the shell shows it: the card
leaves the stage until the author has answered and closed out - see the
next section. A refused reply restores it with the draft kept.

## When a card reaches the stage

Captain-approved on a board in two rounds on 2026-09-27 ("ship it",
verdict "Ship it as recommended"; the decided design is sections 0, 6 and
R2 of `fm3000-card-return-closeout-r1/design-excerpt.md`). It replaced the
renderer's own hide, which brought a card back on its author's FIRST write
after the reply, whatever it said: 10 of 25 answered replies on the
captain's install came back before the answer was settled - 4
acknowledgements ("I'll assess..."), 4 author addenda seconds apart, 2
corrections after a Firstmate steer.

**One rule for every crewmate card** (the captain's Q1 A and Q5 A): a
crewmate's card - new, revised, or answered in its thread - reaches the
stage at the crewmate's CLOSE-OUT after its last write: its next `report`,
or its idle (its resumable turn ending), whichever comes first. Cancellation
and terminal session failure close the task and retire all its open cards,
including hidden replies, Working cards and pending revisions, without
releasing them onto the stage. Card rows, revisions and threads remain on
the record; they do not return after restart. A recoverable provider-failed
turn or interruption is still an idle boundary, not a task close. Emission
also rechecks the task at publication, so a completion check that finishes
after closure cannot recreate a retired choice. A
captain reply takes the card off the stage, and it stays off while his line
is the newest on the thread. Every write in between lands on the record and
paints the thread; the stage does not move. A card already on the stage
that its crewmate revises keeps showing what it showed - a keeps-open
click's Working chip included - and redraws in place at the close-out.

**The Firstmate's own cards** keep working as they did (the captain's Q3
A): they go up and redraw at once, its turn's end is its close-out, and
its closing words are its thread answer - for the reply its turn was about
and, since contract v4.14, for one it read mid-turn - unless it revised the
card. When the answer needs a crewmate, its persona says to say so in the
card and revise the same card when the answer lands, never to answer a
thread with a new card.

**The hidden state lives in the core** (the captain's Q4 A): `Card.awaiting`
on the card snapshot - `answer` while the captain's line is the newest on
the thread, `close-out` while the author has written and not yet closed out,
absent on a card the stage shows. `CardService` is its one writer: the
captain's line sets `answer` (`addMessage`), any later line ends it (the
author's answer, or the host's `revised:` for a revision), every crewmate
write holds a new or hidden card for its close-out, and `closeOut` - called
from the crewmate's `report` and its resumable turn's end, and the
Firstmate's turn end - releases what waited on that author. `snapshot()` is
the stage: a card on it whose author has written again is pushed as the
version the stage showed until the close-out. The column is `cards.awaiting`
(migration 52), so a hide survives a restart and a reload; the restart is
itself every author's close-out, so a card that only waited on one reaches
the stage at boot. A click resolves against the version on the stage.

What reads it: the renderer shows a card only when it is not awaiting
(`visibleCards`) and has no door of its own - a thread message never brings
a card back, and a card's return is an arrival: onto the stage when nothing
else is shown, else behind the shown card, unread, with the notice pulse.
`sendReply` takes the card off the stage at once, as the core's push then
confirms. The native notifier counts a card only once it is on the stage,
so a return notifies like an arrival. Observe and the tests read the same
snapshot.

What does not read it: the whose-turn rule and the idle ladder read the
record, where the card is open from its emit and the captain's line is a
thread fact, exactly as before (R2: "only the stage waits").

**While the author works**: nothing on the stage, and one feed line at
reply time on a crewmate's card - `You asked crewmate N under "<title>"`
through `broadcastEvent` (the captain's Q2 A); a Firstmate card's reply
already has its "Captain: ..." line. The card's return is its own notice.
The task timeline records each crewmate card's stage moment as its
`card_raised` event, written at the close-out with the close-out that
released it (`data.closeOut`: `report`, `idle`, `restart`), and again on a
return after the captain's reply (`data.returned`), so the replay can count
a late return.

**The contract** (v4.14): the crewmate's thread steer preamble and
`CARD_REPLY` say to do the work his words need first, answer once - revise
the card, or reply when nothing on it changes - then report, because the
card comes back when you are done; never acknowledge or announce.

## The contract both agents read

`CARD_REPLY` in `src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts` is ONE text, included
exactly once by every persona beside `CARD_AUTHORING` (the captain's Q4 B:
"this is not just crewmate - firstmate should largely share the same
contract"). It says: revise the card when the reply changes what the card
should say (same id, `emit_card`); answer in prose when nothing on the card
changes; a reply is prose only - no actions, no script, no figure; and a
reply resolves nothing. Since v4.14 it also says when: the work comes
first and the answer once, because the card comes back only when its
author is done. `piResources.test.ts` pins that every persona carries it
once and no tool description repeats a sentence of it, the same structural
pin `CARD_AUTHORING` has.

A crewmate gains one output for that answer: `reply(card_id, text)`
(`crewmateTaskTools.ts`, Claude twin in `claudeTaskTools.ts`), beside
`report` / `emit_card` / `note_progress` / `file_followup`. Its description
carries call mechanics only. The Firstmate's tool count is unchanged at 24
- there is no Firstmate `reply` tool; it answers the same two ways through
`emit_card` and its closing words.

## Firstmate-card threads (phase 2)

A captain reply on the Firstmate's own card is a captain TURN about that
card, not a steer. `cardTakesReplies` is true for a Firstmate author;
`CrewSupervisor.replyToCard` files the captain's message and calls
`converseAboutCard` (`FirstmateAgent.converse` with `aboutCardId`). The
about line replaces the maybe-hint:

`about: card <id> (<presentation>) "<title>" - the captain replied in its thread`

The Firstmate answers through the same `CARD_REPLY` shape: revise the card
under the same id (the host's "revised:" line already records that) or
leave closing words as prose (`recordFirstmateThreadAnswer`, only when the
newest thread message is still the captain's). A parked idle turn keeps the
card on its inbox ref (`captain-turn:card:<id>`); a mid-turn reply rides
the existing steer with the about line in context, and since v4.14 the
turn's closing words answer it too, because the card now waits for an
answer across restarts. Contract v4.2 is unchanged; the wire bump is
protocol 1.19.0 for images on `fm:cards:reply`.

## Images on steers (phase 2)

Pi's `steer(text, images)` already existed. The Claude Agent SDK accepts
the same bytes as user-message image blocks
(`{ type: "image", source: { type: "base64", media_type, data } }`) on
both `prompt` and `steer`. The durable inbox stores text only, so a
copy that cannot keep the bytes says so with that note instead of dropping
them silently; a live native session carries the bytes on the call.

`fm:cards:reply` takes the same union converse does (words, or
`{ text?, images? }`). An image-only reply is stored as `"sent a picture"`.
The reply row pastes pictures the way the main input does. Its field is the
composer's own (`ComposerField`, `docs/composer.md` "The card reply row"):
the same keys, growth to 5 lines, and the count and refusal against
`CARD_REPLY_MAX_CHARS`. Thread messages keep their line breaks.

## Thread in Observe (phase 2)

Observe's session **detail** (not the list) carries `threads`: open cards
on that session that already have a message. The Firstmate session lists
Firstmate-authored cards; a crewmate session lists that task's. Empty
threads stay off the pane. `CardService.observeThreads` is the source;
the frame paints one header line per thread
(`[data-observe-threads]`, `"Title: N · last who"`). Observe remains
dev-only (`docs/dev-observe.md`).

## The settle hand-off, with no classifier

"merge it", "land it", "discard it" typed under a crewmate's card is not the
crewmate's to run, and **nothing in the host reads those words**. The
crewmate's own instruction does the routing: it closes its card and carries
the captain's words verbatim into its `report`, which the whose-turn rule
routes to the Firstmate - the turn that then runs the settle it would have
run had he typed the same words in the main input.

That is the captain's Q2 as he corrected it: "crewmate should not answer the
user with 'not mine'. it should just close the card and pass the decision to
firstmate to execute."

## How the Firstmate learns

It is never woken for a thread message (the captain's C9 A). Two bounded
facts reach it on whatever turn comes next:

- **"thread activity since your last turn"** - a context-block section
  beside `renderCaptainResolutions`, one line per card: who wrote last, the
  first ~120 characters, how many messages, and whether the author still
  owes an answer. Bounded exactly like the resolutions (8 lines, 6 h), with
  the same watermark, so a busy conversation cannot swell the block.
- **`thread:` on the task's crew line** - `2 messages, last from captain`,

The whose-turn rule gains one fact (`reportSort.ts`): an unanswered captain
message in a thread is the CREWMATE's turn, so its report wakes nobody. It
is branch 0, above the open-card branch, deliberately - the captain has
spoken since that card went up, so the card no longer holds the turn.

## The shell

The design skill owns every visual rule

`src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx` implements it and
`threadGeometry.ts` holds the ladder's arithmetic.

While a card has no thread, "reply to this card…" is the very bottom of the
card, under the action row and one hairline above it (the captain's tweak

reply row at all.

The first sent message opens the thread beside the card in ONE container

hairline between the columns, the pair centred as one object. Thread
`clamp(0.4 × stage, 288, 360)`, card `min(W, stage − 32 − thread)`, where W
is the card's own width - 560 for a regular card, more for a wide or full
one or one the captain dragged (`docs/card-authoring.md` "Card width").

When the pair would leave the card under 400px the docked panels FOLD (tweak
2): `html[data-rails-folded]` gives the rails' width back to the stage and a
4px edge tab at each folded side says the panels are one click away - the
click closes the thread, which returns them. Fold is not collapse: a
collapsed dock still holds its full `--rail-width`, so collapsing frees
nothing. The rails keep their panels while folded, which is why
`--rail-docked-*` (what they ask for) is a different variable from
`--occupied-rail-*` (what they take): reading the effective one would make
the ladder circular and the pair would oscillate.

In place is the last rung - a segmented control in the card's head swaps the
body for the message list - and needs a stage under 720px, which the app's
own 960px window minimum puts out of reach.

`threadGeometry.test.ts` is the binding evidence: the R3.1 table at 960 /
1200 / 1440 / 1728 with both docks, one dock and none, and
`card-threads.spec.ts` measures the real shell against it - folded at the
default 1200 (both docks occupied leave a 600px stage) and beside the docks
at 1728, clear of the rail.

One sharp edge paid for there: `--rail-docked-left|right` are REGISTERED
(`@property`, `syntax: "<length>"`) because the ladder reads them. An
unregistered custom property computes to its own token stream, so
`--rail-docked-left: var(--rail-width)` reads back through
`getComputedStyle` as the literal `max(300px, 20vw)` and parses as `NaN`;
the ladder then placed the pair as if nothing were docked and it sat under
the rail. `useShellLayout` also observes the STAGE's size, because a rail
docking or undocking is not a render of the card layer.

## Ready decisions and choice admission

Task waiting follows the version the stage shows, not the durable head
(`docs/task-record.md`, "Ready waiting is a presentation projection"). New
crewmate cards still release at report or idle, whichever comes first; report
can release a decision while its author keeps working. A reply hides it at
once. Acknowledgement or an unreleased revision does not bring it back. An
unanswered reply stays hidden across restart; restart releases close-out and
resets Working to ready. These release and durable-gate policies are unchanged.

Other thrown action/reply refusals keep their reason, but the preload removes
Electron's remote-method wrapper and error-class prefix before the shell or an
embedded card receives them (`src/preload/cardRequest.ts`). A failure with no
usable reason gets a short choice/reply-specific fallback. This does not change
acceptance receipts, the wire contract, or the shell's refusal recovery: choices
stay open and replies return with their unsent words and pictures kept.

A hidden, Working or associated closed-task card refuses an action before
resolution, author guidance or an effect. A choice naming no action declared
by the shown offer also refuses before bookkeeping, leaving both the card and
its task open; an unseen action from a pending revision is not yet offered.
Refusal is typed internally and transported as `refusal` text, not the empty
acceptance receipt: the shell retains an open card and shows the refusal
without a transport wrapper, rather than removing it optimistically. Valid
choices still use the shown offer, including when a newer stored revision
changes its actions.
Gate-backed decisions/operations use their existing typed card-raised task
association after closure (closure clears the live gate). Submission metadata,
required-answer rules and routing are unchanged. Cancellation and terminal
session failure retire the task's open cards through `SettleService.closeRecord`,
as ordinary settle closure does through `closeTask`.

- `tests/e2e/task-card-retirement.spec.ts` - a shown decision disappears on
  running cancellation or actual terminal client exit and stays retired after
  restart; cancellation of a restored idle task retires its decision without
  reopening the session. `crewSupervisor.test.ts` joins closure with cards and
  task detail, covering hidden/Working cards, pending revisions, preserved
  history/threads, unrelated choices and resumable failure/interruption.

  revises the card in place, a reply answered in the thread, and "merge it"
  under a completion card landing as the Firstmate's settle) plus phase 2:
  a captain reply on a Firstmate card revises it / lands as prose, and an
  image rides a thread reply on a transport that supports it. The stage
  rule's case A: an acknowledgement leaves the card off the stage, a reload
  keeps it off, and the report brings it back, answered.

  crewmate's own reply, the whose-turn fact, the context facts, a Firstmate
  card routing to a captain turn, and an image on a crewmate steer.
- `firstmateAgent.test.ts` - the about-card line and the prose capture at
  turn end.
- `cardStore.test.ts`, `reportSort.test.ts`, `threadGeometry.test.ts`,
  `observeService.test.ts` / `observe.frame.test.ts` (threads on the
  detail header).

**The hidden state lives in the core** (the captain's Q4 A): `Card.awaiting`
on the card snapshot - `answer` while the captain's line is the newest on
the thread, `close-out` while the author has written and not yet closed out,
absent on a card the stage shows. `CardService` is its one writer: the
captain's line sets `answer` (`addMessage`), any later line ends it (the
author's answer, or the host's `revised:` for a revision), every crewmate
write holds a new or hidden card for its close-out, and `closeOut` - called
from the crewmate's `report` and its resumable turn's end, and the
Firstmate's turn end - releases what waited on that author. `snapshot()` is
the stage: a card on it whose author has written again is pushed as the
version the stage showed until the close-out. The column is `cards.awaiting`
(migration 52), so a hide survives a restart and a reload; the restart is
itself every author's close-out, so a card that only waited on one reaches
the stage at boot. A click resolves against the version on the stage.

What reads it: the renderer shows a card only when it is not awaiting
(`visibleCards`) and has no door of its own - a thread message never brings
a card back, and a card's return is an arrival: onto the stage when nothing
else is shown, else behind the shown card, unread, with the notice pulse.
`sendReply` takes the card off the stage at once, as the core's push then
confirms. The native notifier counts a card only once it is on the stage,
so a return notifies like an arrival. Observe and the tests read the same
snapshot.

What does not read it: the whose-turn rule and the idle ladder read the
record, where the card is open from its emit and the captain's line is a
thread fact, exactly as before (R2: "only the stage waits").

**While the author works**: nothing on the stage, and one feed line at
reply time on a crewmate's card - `You asked crewmate N under "<title>"`
through `broadcastEvent` (the captain's Q2 A); a Firstmate card's reply
already has its "Captain: ..." line. The card's return is its own notice.
The task timeline records each crewmate card's stage moment as its
`card_raised` event, written at the close-out with the close-out that
released it (`data.closeOut`: `report`, `idle`, `restart`), and again on a
return after the captain's reply (`data.returned`), so the replay can count
a late return.

**The contract** (v4.14): the crewmate's thread steer preamble and
`CARD_REPLY` say to do the work his words need first, answer once - revise
the card, or reply when nothing on it changes - then report, because the
card comes back when you are done; never acknowledge or announce.

## The contract both agents read

`CARD_REPLY` in `src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts` is ONE text, included
exactly once by every persona beside `CARD_AUTHORING` (the captain's Q4 B:
"this is not just crewmate - firstmate should largely share the same
contract"). It says: revise the card when the reply changes what the card
should say (same id, `emit_card`); answer in prose when nothing on the card
changes; a reply is prose only - no actions, no script, no figure; and a
reply resolves nothing. Since v4.14 it also says when: the work comes
first and the answer once, because the card comes back only when its
author is done. `piResources.test.ts` pins that every persona carries it
once and no tool description repeats a sentence of it, the same structural
pin `CARD_AUTHORING` has.

A crewmate gains one output for that answer: `reply(card_id, text)`
(`crewmateTaskTools.ts`, Claude twin in `claudeTaskTools.ts`), beside
`report` / `emit_card` / `note_progress` / `file_followup`. Its description
carries call mechanics only. The Firstmate's tool count is unchanged at 24
- there is no Firstmate `reply` tool; it answers the same two ways through
`emit_card` and its closing words.

## Firstmate-card threads (phase 2)

A captain reply on the Firstmate's own card is a captain TURN about that
card, not a steer. `cardTakesReplies` is true for a Firstmate author;
`CrewSupervisor.replyToCard` files the captain's message and calls
`converseAboutCard` (`FirstmateAgent.converse` with `aboutCardId`). The
about line replaces the maybe-hint:

`about: card <id> (<presentation>) "<title>" - the captain replied in its thread`

The Firstmate answers through the same `CARD_REPLY` shape: revise the card
under the same id (the host's "revised:" line already records that) or
leave closing words as prose (`recordFirstmateThreadAnswer`, only when the
newest thread message is still the captain's). A parked idle turn keeps the
card on its inbox ref (`captain-turn:card:<id>`); a mid-turn reply rides
the existing steer with the about line in context, and since v4.14 the
turn's closing words answer it too, because the card now waits for an
answer across restarts. Contract v4.2 is unchanged; the wire bump is
protocol 1.19.0 for images on `fm:cards:reply`.

## Images on steers (phase 2)

Pi's `steer(text, images)` already existed. The Claude Agent SDK accepts
the same bytes as user-message image blocks
(`{ type: "image", source: { type: "base64", media_type, data } }`) on
both `prompt` and `steer`. The durable inbox stores text only, so a
copy that cannot keep the bytes says so with that note instead of dropping
them silently; a live native session carries the bytes on the call.

`fm:cards:reply` takes the same union converse does (words, or
`{ text?, images? }`). An image-only reply is stored as `"sent a picture"`.
The reply row pastes pictures the way the main input does. Its field is the
composer's own (`ComposerField`, `docs/composer.md` "The card reply row"):
the same keys, growth to 5 lines, and the count and refusal against
`CARD_REPLY_MAX_CHARS`. Thread messages keep their line breaks.

## Thread in Observe (phase 2)

Observe's session **detail** (not the list) carries `threads`: open cards
on that session that already have a message. The Firstmate session lists
Firstmate-authored cards; a crewmate session lists that task's. Empty
threads stay off the pane. `CardService.observeThreads` is the source;
the frame paints one header line per thread
(`[data-observe-threads]`, `"Title: N · last who"`). Observe remains
dev-only (`docs/dev-observe.md`).

## The settle hand-off, with no classifier

"merge it", "land it", "discard it" typed under a crewmate's card is not the
crewmate's to run, and **nothing in the host reads those words**. The
crewmate's own instruction does the routing: it closes its card and carries
the captain's words verbatim into its `report`, which the whose-turn rule
routes to the Firstmate - the turn that then runs the settle it would have
run had he typed the same words in the main input.

That is the captain's Q2 as he corrected it: "crewmate should not answer the
user with 'not mine'. it should just close the card and pass the decision to
firstmate to execute."

## How the Firstmate learns

It is never woken for a thread message (the captain's C9 A). Two bounded
facts reach it on whatever turn comes next:

- **"thread activity since your last turn"** - a context-block section
  beside `renderCaptainResolutions`, one line per card: who wrote last, the
  first ~120 characters, how many messages, and whether the author still
  owes an answer. Bounded exactly like the resolutions (8 lines, 6 h), with
  the same watermark, so a busy conversation cannot swell the block.
- **`thread:` on the task's crew line** - `2 messages, last from captain`,
  from `CardService.threadFact`; `crew_status` carries the same field.

The whose-turn rule gains one fact (`reportSort.ts`): an unanswered captain
message in a thread is the CREWMATE's turn, so its report wakes nobody. It
is branch 0, above the open-card branch, deliberately - the captain has
spoken since that card went up, so the card no longer holds the turn.

## The shell

The design skill owns every visual rule
(`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/cards/CardThread.prompt.md`);
`src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx` implements it and
`threadGeometry.ts` holds the ladder's arithmetic.

While a card has no thread, "reply to this card…" is the very bottom of the
card, under the action row and one hairline above it (the captain's tweak
3). A card with no author to reach - the host's own agent-down set - has no
reply row at all.

The first sent message opens the thread beside the card in ONE container
(tweak 1): one surface, border, radius and shadow, a single `--line-2`
hairline between the columns, the pair centred as one object. Thread
`clamp(0.4 × stage, 288, 360)`, card `min(W, stage − 32 − thread)`, where W
is the card's own width - 560 for a regular card, more for a wide or full
one or one the captain dragged (`docs/card-authoring.md` "Card width").

When the pair would leave the card under 400px the docked panels FOLD (tweak
2): `html[data-rails-folded]` gives the rails' width back to the stage and a
4px edge tab at each folded side says the panels are one click away - the
click closes the thread, which returns them. Fold is not collapse: a
collapsed dock still holds its full `--rail-width`, so collapsing frees
nothing. The rails keep their panels while folded, which is why
`--rail-docked-*` (what they ask for) is a different variable from
`--occupied-rail-*` (what they take): reading the effective one would make
the ladder circular and the pair would oscillate.

In place is the last rung - a segmented control in the card's head swaps the
body for the message list - and needs a stage under 720px, which the app's
own 960px window minimum puts out of reach.

`threadGeometry.test.ts` is the binding evidence: the R3.1 table at 960 /
1200 / 1440 / 1728 with both docks, one dock and none, and
`card-threads.spec.ts` measures the real shell against it - folded at the
default 1200 (both docks occupied leave a 600px stage) and beside the docks
at 1728, clear of the rail.

One sharp edge paid for there: `--rail-docked-left|right` are REGISTERED
(`@property`, `syntax: "<length>"`) because the ladder reads them. An
unregistered custom property computes to its own token stream, so
`--rail-docked-left: var(--rail-width)` reads back through
`getComputedStyle` as the literal `max(300px, 20vw)` and parses as `NaN`;
the ladder then placed the pair as if nothing were docked and it sat under
the rail. `useShellLayout` also observes the STAGE's size, because a rail
docking or undocking is not a render of the card layer.

## Ready decisions and choice admission

Task waiting follows the version the stage shows, not the durable head
(`docs/task-record.md`, "Ready waiting is a presentation projection"). New
crewmate cards still release at report or idle, whichever comes first; report
can release a decision while its author keeps working. A reply hides it at
once. Acknowledgement or an unreleased revision does not bring it back. An
unanswered reply stays hidden across restart; restart releases close-out and
resets Working to ready. These release and durable-gate policies are unchanged.

Other thrown action/reply refusals keep their reason, but the preload removes
Electron's remote-method wrapper and error-class prefix before the shell or an
embedded card receives them (`src/preload/cardRequest.ts`). A failure with no
usable reason gets a short choice/reply-specific fallback. This does not change
acceptance receipts, the wire contract, or the shell's refusal recovery: choices
stay open and replies return with their unsent words and pictures kept.

A hidden, Working or associated closed-task card refuses an action before
resolution, author guidance or an effect. A choice naming no action declared
by the shown offer also refuses before bookkeeping, leaving both the card and
its task open; an unseen action from a pending revision is not yet offered.
Refusal is typed internally and transported as `refusal` text, not the empty
acceptance receipt: the shell retains an open card and shows the refusal
without a transport wrapper, rather than removing it optimistically. Valid
choices still use the shown offer, including when a newer stored revision
changes its actions.
Gate-backed decisions/operations use their existing typed card-raised task
association after closure (closure clears the live gate). Submission metadata,
required-answer rules and routing are unchanged. Cancellation and terminal
session failure retire the task's open cards through `SettleService.closeRecord`,
as ordinary settle closure does through `closeTask`.

  running cancellation or actual terminal client exit and stays retired after
  restart; cancellation of a restored idle task retires its decision without
  reopening the session. `crewSupervisor.test.ts` joins closure with cards and

- `cardStore.test.ts`, `reportSort.test.ts`, `threadGeometry.test.ts`,

import { type PluginManifest, parsePluginManifest } from "@shared/plugins/manifest";
import { BUILTIN_SURFACES } from "@shared/surfaces";

/**
 * The app's own UI, declared as the first plugin (docs/ui-plugins.md).
 * Everything here is data the registries read; the React that serves the
 * settings sections is bound in ./index.ts. Parsing at module load means a
 * malformed built-in manifest fails the first render and the unit test,
 * never a user's session.
 *
 * Card kinds: the three PRESENTATIONS a wire card derives (cards/tasks/
 * agents P1, `cardPresentation` in cards.ts - a decision has actions, a
 * note none, an attention is the host's own), plus the host-owned
 * `task-record` (task-system P4). Nothing on the wire declares a kind: the
 * card layer derives the presentation and reads its dress here. The chrome
 * and body policy that used to be three switch statements in the card
 * layer live here as rows; every card renders its frame from the first
 * byte. A row says only how a STREAMING body is shown - there is no body
 * profile any more, because there is no sanitizer (captain decision,
 * 2026-09-15): every body renders as its author wrote it, inside the
 * unchanged sandbox and CSP. `task-record` is never persisted in `cards` and never emitted by an
 * agent (`cardsSnapshotSchema` refuses anything but the one card shape),
 * so its body policy is moot - the body is a template the host mounts for
 * the open task (./record).
 *
 * Side panels (phase 2): the activity feed rides the left rail as a Tier-2
 * frame. The right rail carries the now panel (P4): what IS, minimal by
 * default, the one panel the captain chose for it (decision D3).
 *
 * Capabilities: the reads the frames subscribe to. Declared like any plugin
 * would, so the host refuses a frame anything it did not ask for.
 */
export const BUILTIN_PLUGIN_ID = "firstmate";

export const builtinManifest: PluginManifest = parsePluginManifest({
  id: BUILTIN_PLUGIN_ID,
  name: "Firstmate 3000",
  // Versions with the app; the field earns its keep on installed plugins,
  // where a capability diff between versions re-runs consent.
  version: "1.0.0",
  contributes: {
    cardKinds: [
      { kind: "decision", chrome: "decision", body: { streaming: "html" } },
      { kind: "note", chrome: "note", body: { streaming: "html" } },
      { kind: "attention", chrome: "attention", body: { streaming: "html" } },
      { kind: "task-record", chrome: "record", body: { streaming: "html" } },
    ],
    settingsSections: [
      { id: "general", label: "General", order: 10, width: "wide" },
      { id: "projects", label: "Projects", order: 15, width: "wide" },
      // "Intelligence", not "Subscriptions" (the captain's Q1 note, S7):
      // the tab holds the accounts, the model board and the Decisions
      // group, and only some of that is a subscription. The id, the
      // `open subscriptions` card effect and the e2e ids are unchanged.
      { id: "subscriptions", label: "Intelligence", order: 20, width: "wide" },
      // Local-dev only (docs/dev-observe.md); the binding's gate decides.
      { id: "observe", label: "Observe", order: 30, width: "wide" },
    ],
    // Declared once for the renderer and the core alike (src/shared/
    // surfaces.ts): the Firstmate's "your surfaces" section and its
    // `personalize` tool name these panels by the same ids.
    sidePanels: [...BUILTIN_SURFACES],
  },
  capabilities: {
    reads: [
      "observe.sessions",
      "observe.session",
      "observe.live",
      // Observe's fourth kind (Step 5): the personal mounts, and whether
      // the host-owned switch has them off at all.
      "personal.mounts",
      "shell.preferences",
      "feed.recent",
      "tasks.board",
      "tasks.detail",
    ],
  },
});
