How Firstmate communicates: a card, never a chat bubble. ONE card shape; the chip is derived from what the card is, never declared: `decision` (chip "Decision", accent) has actions and asks the user to choose; `note` (chip "Note", neutral) has none and states a fact; `attention` (chip "Attention", danger) is the app's own card when no agent can answer - a provider needs sign in, Firstmate is out of quota or hit an error, or a crewmate has stayed stuck through a nudge and two unanswered wakes (the stall card: "<task> has been stuck for 1h 20m", with Continue, Stop it and a danger Discard); `working` while a card revises; plus `record` - a task's record (status pill in the task popover; body `TaskRecord`; never any card actions - its footer is the host's lifecycle toggles, Drop task / Start / Stop it / Continue, and put in, discard and keep stay on cards). A working preview is a decision whose body is interactive, not a kind of its own.
Every card is the head of a thread with its author and carries a reply row; the thread's own rules are `CardThread.prompt.md`, and a card with a thread open is one column of a single container rather than a surface of its own.
A card whose author ran on a model names it as the model chip (`ModelChip`, `../core/Badge.prompt.md`) right after the meta line: the meta line and the chip share the room between the kind chip and close, and the meta line is the one that gives way (ellipsis); the chip keeps its whole name, never cut and never pushed past close, wrapping inside itself only when the name is longer than all the room there is. The model rides as its own field, never inside the meta text.
Every card has a top-right close control (IconButton, aria-label Close). Close dismisses the card; it is not a footer action. Notes with no declared actions have no Done button.
Card actions acknowledge before the next paint: while the host accepts a request, the selected Button is pending and the entire action row is disabled. Embedded body actions use the same request guard. Acceptance closes the card before background work settles; the durable feed carries the outcome, including refusal reasons. A close is a receipt for the choice, not proof of success. See `../core/Button.prompt.md` for pending and inline request-error treatment.
A decision's footer reads left to right: any non-closing (`keeps_open`) action as a ghost button - offered only when a choice is genuinely non-closing, never as a default addition - the other choices (secondary; a destructive one such as Discard in `danger`), and the emitter's one default (primary) - the only primary on the card, unless the default is itself destructive, in which case danger wins. There is no automatic Later and no Keep button: closing the card is keep. Keep `--space-3` above the action row so the body and buttons stay distinct. The footer is two non-wrapping groups, quiet (the ghosts) then choices, in a right-aligned wrapping row: when the card is too narrow for one row the choices move down together, and the default never sits alone on a row. A ghost action does not close the card: while the emitter revises it the chip reads "Working" and every footer Button is disabled (no pending label, nothing shifts); the revised body arrives in place and the footer re-enables.
A decision may ask several questions in its body, as ordinary named form controls the author presents as it likes (a radio group, checkboxes, a select, a text field; the question worded in its `fieldset`'s `legend`, or a lone field's bound `<label>`; short, stable names and values; the proposed option checked, `required` on a must-pick, a bound `<label>` per option; `docs/card-authoring.md` "Questions in the body"). A pick never sends anything: the footer's queue group - the first thing in the action row, pushed left, `--font-mono` `--text-xs` `--fg-3`, `aria-live="polite"` - counts them as "2 of 3 answered", with " · 1 changed" once an answer differs from the proposal, and is absent on a card whose body asks nothing. A closing choice stays disabled until every question has an answer; a `keeps_open` choice sends what there is. When the captain closes with a changed answer, the action row becomes one question in the card instead - "You changed 2 answers. Closing does not send them." (`--text-sm`, `--fg-2`, left) with `secondary` "Keep answering" and primary "Close" on the right - and nothing else asks. The frame stylesheet dresses a plain `fieldset` as a hairline `--line-1` box at `--radius-m` with its `legend` in `--fg-1` weight 500, each radio or checkbox label a row with `--space-2` between control and text (`accent-color: --accent`, a checked row's text `--fg-1`), and a `textarea` full width under its label.
Every ready card body is semantic HTML in a sandboxed iframe. The host owns the chip, title, close, pager, and footer actions. Follow the card contract the models read (`CARD_AUTHORING` in `src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts`, mirrored by the readme's Card bodies bullet): a card leads with its answer in one sentence (finished code-work completion cards are the exception: the title alone carries the answer, and the body opens at Why, then What changed, Before and After; `docs/card-authoring.md` owns that loose outline), and an answer that explains how something works, compares options, or shows state, shape or layout is drawn - that sentence, then the figures carrying it. An explanation with several parts gets several figures, each beside the short sentence it illustrates, rather than one crowded drawing. Keep prose needed to follow the answer in the open; reserve `<details>` for evidence, exact code paths, qualifications, and other material for a reader who digs. Figures are free-form and all of SVG renders. No shape is prescribed. Give each SVG a `viewBox`, 510 units wide with `width="100%"` when it is full width, or its pixel width when it is smaller so the card only shrinks it; use theme tokens so it follows light and dark, `--accent` for the single most-current or lit element within each figure - one accent per figure, not one per card - non-accent tokens for everything else it draws, and `--ok`, `--warn`, or `--danger` only for real state. A picture never reaches past the body's width; one that would stand taller than 360 px shrinks to fit 360 px, whole, letterboxed on `--bg-1` - never cropped. Several in a `figure.fm-pictures` are a group, lead and strip: the first leads, the rest are 88 x 60 thumbnails cropped to their top, five shown and a mono `+N` tile for the rest, the `figcaption` under them; the frame stylesheet draws all of it, so a group of the body's own `data:` pictures looks the same. A click on any picture, or on a group's `+N` tile, opens the picture viewer over the window, paging within that group (`PictureViewer.prompt.md`). A card carrying a settle effect ends with the host-rendered `.fm-facts` strip (project, crewmate model, posture, PR link, CI state, any round caps the host has counted, and the review on a reviewed task) that the body never repeats. A body's own inline script may add behavior (a canvas, a toggle) but loads nothing; if it stops answering, the body becomes one `--fg-3` / `--text-sm` line, "This card stopped responding.", with a `secondary` `sm` Retry Button on the same row - no icon, no danger color, chrome unchanged.
A card is one of three widths, never a setting: regular 560, wide 800, full the stage up to 1040, each clamped to the stage less 32 px as 560 always was. The host decides at emit from closed facts about the body - wide for a table of 4+ columns, a `<pre>` line over 60 characters, a picture 900 px or wider, a picture group or a preview; full for a picture 1,600 px or wider or a table of 6+ columns - and the author's `width` hint can only widen it. The captain drags either edge, 480 to full, and the card grows from its centre by twice the pointer's travel; the drag holds while the card is up and through its revisions, and a double click returns the decided width. Each edge is a 12 px `role="separator"` strip ("Resize card", arrow keys move 16 px) whose grip - a 4 x 32 `--accent` pill, `--radius-pill` - shows only while the edge is hovered, held or focused. A lone card stays centred on the window and moves off it only as far as it must to clear a docked rail. When the docked stage cannot give a card wider than regular 720 px (or what it asks, if less) and a dock is occupied, the docks fold as they do for a thread, with the same edge tabs, and unfold when the card leaves; a tab click returns the card to regular. Width changes - paging, a revision, the fold - move over `--dur-med` `--ease-out`; a drag follows the pointer, and a resized window or dock is followed at once, so a card never reaches under a rail while it catches up. Inside the body, prose (paragraphs, lists, headings, captions, summaries) keeps a 66-character measure in any width while tables, code, picture groups and figures take the room, and a `width="100%"` drawing is capped at its own viewBox units, so a 510-unit figure draws 1:1 in a wide card rather than growing with it. The body's document carries `data-width` (`regular`, `wide`, `full`) for the size it is shown at.
```jsx
<ResponseCard kind="decision" title="Two ways to fix the flaky test" meta="just now" onClose={onClose}
  actions={<><Button variant="secondary">Mock the clock</Button><Button>Await the queue</Button></>}>
  <iframe title="Two ways to fix the flaky test body" sandbox="allow-scripts" srcDoc={bodyDocument} />
</ResponseCard>
```
Wraps the one visible ResponseCard; ghost edges peek above when more cards wait, with prev/next + "2 / 5".
```jsx
<CardStack index={i} count={5} unreadBefore={0} unreadAfter={1} onPrev={p} onNext={n}><ResponseCard …/></CardStack>
```
Cards are prioritized by importance; only one is ever shown. The stack is as wide as the shown card (`ResponseCard.prompt.md`, widths): its peeks and pager follow that card, and paging between a regular and a wide card moves the edges over `--dur-med`.

A new card never steals the shown one - it lands on the stack unseen, and the pager says so: an `--accent` dot (6px, `--radius-pill`, ringed in `--bg-0`) on the arrow that leads to it, and one accent mono Badge "1 new" beside the pager, positioned outside the centred arrow group so the arrows never move under the pointer. A card counts as seen once it has been the shown card; the dot and the badge leave when nothing unseen remains. No animation on the badge: the Firstmate's notice pulse is the motion.

Notes are the one kind that step aside on their own: a note already seen, on a task, and older than the stack's threshold collapses out of the stack into its task record (the answer's body is kept there). Decisions, results, and prototypes never collapse; an unseen note never does either.
The body of a task's record popover. Its top row is the status pill, the task key, and the assigned model as its chip (`ModelChip`: the outline Badge in mono) beside the key, then close; the title sits alone beneath at `--text-lg`, the decision card's title size. The pill is neutral with the Tasks rail's own dot for the task (ember working, cyan idle, lava interrupted, hollow with no crewmate); the whole pill tints only when the state needs the captain's eye - `accent` for waiting on you, `danger` for interrupted or failed. The key gives way (ellipsis) before the chip does; a chip with no room beside the key takes the next line of the top row, whole. It opens at its fully measured natural height, clamped to the window, with no entrance or height animation; loading content is measured before the pane is revealed.

**Its buttons are lifecycle toggles only; judgment calls stay on cards** (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28, reversing the 2026-09-09 read-only record; Drop task added for never-started work, FI3-243). A footer in the card footer's pattern - right-aligned, the one primary last, `--space-3` above - offers exactly what the task's typed state calls for: `Drop task` (secondary) on open work that has never started, immediately before `Start` when Start applies, and alone when it does not (a parent, when-ready work, a blocked row whose Start is disabled). `Start` (primary) on charted work on request; `Start` disabled with "Waits on FI3-x" (`--text-sm`, `--fg-3`, left) while something blocks it; `Stop it` (secondary) on live work; `Stop it` then `Continue` (primary) on interrupted work; nothing on closed work, or while a decision card waits on work that has already started (the body's box offers `Show the card`, a secondary button that brings that card forward and writes nothing). The top-right cross is `Hide`: it dismisses the popover and never drops the task. Drop task and Stop it each ask once, inline: the row becomes "Drop FI3-x? It won't start. Its record stays." or "Stop FI3-x? It ends the task and keeps a copy of its unfinished work." (`--text-sm`, `--fg-2`, left). Drop task's confirm is the danger outline, Cancel is secondary and takes focus, and Enter does not approve. Confirmation names tasks still waiting on this work and says dropping will not start them. A parent with open parts is refused in plain words; nothing is written. Cancel, or hiding the popover, writes nothing. A click is pending until the record moves under it, and competing buttons disable immediately. A refusal is inline and writes nothing. Merge, discard and keep are never here. Every other write to a task happens by talking to Firstmate while the card is open (the open card is what points the turn at this task).

Waiting uses only `waitingCardId`, the reachable shown ready decision on a live
task, not `flags.needsYou` (broader attention). Reply hides and refusal
restorations update the open record with the rail. No ready choice means
existing attention/hold guidance and lifecycle controls, not a decision claim.
An interruption or blocker may remain the primary explanation while a
simultaneous ready choice still has Show the card. That route refreshes the
choice before focusing it, never forcing a hidden card onto the stage.

The body leads with the current facts: the headline at `--text-base` under a micro label that carries its stamp (`LATEST REPORT · 3 min ago`) - the report's own one-line summary, newer progress, or for a closed row how it closed (`Dropped 1 hr ago: <the words it was dropped with>`); an attention box when something is wrong (danger-tinted, in plain words, for an interrupted or failed task); one positive sentence of typed state (`Waiting on the checks for pull request #422. Nothing needs you.`, `Merged 46 min ago as pull request #417. The checks passed.`); and the live change with its checks. A crew filing's reason leads only while it is charted. Then the record, as peer rows that each open on their own, painted like the panel `Disclosure` (micro label, mono count, caret), each absent when empty: Goal and your words (the goal in `--fg-1`, a filing's "Why it was filed" once it has left the charted state, the captain's words verbatim in a hairline blockquote, later asks) · Full report (absent when it only repeats the headline) · Activity (the timeline condensed by kind in plain words, newest last, short relative ages in mono, a plain `Show earlier · N` link above when it is longer) · Details (a labeled list: Crewmate `crewmate 21 on GPT-6 Sol`, Project, Branch, Delivery `As a pull request · care: Default`, and the related work). Every time reads relative, the absolute time on hover. No row nests another disclosure.

```jsx
<ResponseCard kind="record" title="Refactor the auth middleware" meta="FM3K-9 · underway" onClose={onClose}>
  <TaskRecord record={{goal:"The middleware has one code path and the suite is green.",userWords:"commission a crewmate: refactor the auth middleware",
    blockedBy:[],blocks:["FM3K-11"],children:{total:1,closed:0},outcome:"Steady as she goes. 14 files changed, tests green.",
    events:[{id:1,at:Date.now()-900000,text:"created"},{id:2,at:Date.now()-800000,text:"dispatched to crewmate 1"},{id:3,at:Date.now(),text:"reported: Steady as she goes."}],
    delivery:{mode:"direct-pr",ci:"green"}}}/>
</ResponseCard>
```

Never persisted as a card, never emitted by an agent, never a feed line: it is a view of the record, opened from a now-panel row and gone when closed. In the app the body is a Tier-2 frame template (`src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/record/`) fed by the `tasks.detail` read, not this JSX; the look is the same.

Its top row is the status pill, the task key, and the assigned model as its chip (`ModelChip`: the outline Badge in mono) beside the key, then close; the title sits alone beneath at `--text-lg`, the decision card's title size. The pill is neutral with the Tasks rail's own dot for the task (ember working, cyan idle, lava interrupted, hollow with no crewmate); the whole pill tints only when the state needs the captain's eye - `accent` for waiting on you, `danger` for interrupted or failed. The key gives way (ellipsis) before the chip does; a chip with no room beside the key takes the next line of the top row, whole. It opens at its fully measured natural height, clamped to the window, with no entrance or height animation; loading content is measured before the pane is revealed.

**Its buttons are lifecycle toggles only; judgment calls stay on cards** (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28, reversing the 2026-09-09 read-only record; Drop task added for never-started work, FI3-243). A footer in the card footer's pattern - right-aligned, the one primary last, `--space-3` above - offers exactly what the task's typed state calls for: `Drop task` (secondary) on open work that has never started, immediately before `Start` when Start applies, and alone when it does not (a parent, when-ready work, a blocked row whose Start is disabled). `Start` (primary) on charted work on request; `Start` disabled with "Waits on FI3-x" (`--text-sm`, `--fg-3`, left) while something blocks it; `Stop it` (secondary) on live work; `Stop it` then `Continue` (primary) on interrupted work; nothing on closed work, or while a decision card waits on work that has already started (the body's box offers `Show the card`, a secondary button that brings that card forward and writes nothing). The top-right cross is `Hide`: it dismisses the popover and never drops the task. Drop task and Stop it each ask once, inline: the row becomes "Drop FI3-x? It won't start. Its record stays." or "Stop FI3-x? It ends the task and keeps a copy of its unfinished work." (`--text-sm`, `--fg-2`, left). Drop task's confirm is the danger outline, Cancel is secondary and takes focus, and Enter does not approve. Confirmation names tasks still waiting on this work and says dropping will not start them. A parent with open parts is refused in plain words; nothing is written. Cancel, or hiding the popover, writes nothing. A click is pending until the record moves under it, and competing buttons disable immediately. A refusal is inline and writes nothing. Merge, discard and keep are never here. Every other write to a task happens by talking to Firstmate while the card is open (the open card is what points the turn at this task).

Waiting uses only `waitingCardId`, the reachable shown ready decision on a live
task, not `flags.needsYou` (broader attention). Reply hides and refusal
restorations update the open record with the rail. No ready choice means
existing attention/hold guidance and lifecycle controls, not a decision claim.
An interruption or blocker may remain the primary explanation while a
simultaneous ready choice still has Show the card. That route refreshes the
choice before focusing it, never forcing a hidden card onto the stage.

The body leads with the current facts: the headline at `--text-base` under a micro label that carries its stamp (`LATEST REPORT · 3 min ago`) - the report's own one-line summary, newer progress, or for a closed row how it closed (`Dropped 1 hr ago: <the words it was dropped with>`); an attention box when something is wrong (danger-tinted, in plain words, for an interrupted or failed task); one positive sentence of typed state (`Waiting on the checks for pull request #422. Nothing needs you.`, `Merged 46 min ago as pull request #417. The checks passed.`); and the live change with its checks. A crew filing's reason leads only while it is charted. Then the record, as peer rows that each open on their own, painted like the panel `Disclosure` (micro label, mono count, caret), each absent when empty: Goal and your words (the goal in `--fg-1`, a filing's "Why it was filed" once it has left the charted state, the captain's words verbatim in a hairline blockquote, later asks) · Full report (absent when it only repeats the headline) · Activity (the timeline condensed by kind in plain words, newest last, short relative ages in mono, a plain `Show earlier · N` link above when it is longer) · Details (a labeled list: Crewmate `crewmate 21 on GPT-6 Sol`, Project, Branch, Delivery `As a pull request · care: Default`, and the related work). Every time reads relative, the absolute time on hover. No row nests another disclosure.

  <TaskRecord record={{goal:"The middleware has one code path and the suite is green.",userWords:"commission a crewmate: refactor the auth middleware",
    blockedBy:[],blocks:["FM3K-11"],children:{total:1,closed:0},outcome:"Steady as she goes. 14 files changed, tests green.",

    delivery:{mode:"direct-pr",ci:"green"}}}/>

Never persisted as a card, never emitted by an agent, never a feed line: it is a view of the record, opened from a now-panel row and gone when closed. In the app the body is a Tier-2 frame template (`src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/record/`) fed by the `tasks.detail` read, not this JSX; the look is the same.

# Firstmate 3000 — Design System

Firstmate 3000 is an AI assistant for software development and general knowledge work, shipped as an Electron desktop app (light + dark theme, dark default). The product feeling: **calm, peaceful, confident, futuristic, a bit of space-travel fantasy, minimal, distraction-free**.

## Product concepts
- **The input** — the default state of the app is a single text input. Placeholder: `press/hold [keybind] to talk` (default keybind: right ⌥, quick press to toggle or hold to talk). It takes more than one line: the pill grows upward into a rounded rectangle as the draft grows, and the stage (the Firstmate and the card) lifts with it (`components/voice/VoiceInput.prompt.md`). Activated, its foot row becomes a live waveform with three controls: abandon (left end), accept, submit (rightmost), while the draft stays on screen.
- **The first launch** (captain decisions 2026-09-19; the app's `docs/first-launch.md`) — while no subscription can serve Firstmate, the null state carries one caption under the character in the reserved null-state display type, "Connect a subscription to begin", one sentence naming the providers that can serve Firstmate itself (Codex, Grok, Claude, or OpenRouter with an API key), and the provider chip row (`components/core/ConnectChips`) so the sign-in happens right there; the input is `disabled` and dimmed with the line "connect a subscription first", and voice-key presses are ignored. It is state, not a flag: it returns if the last such subscription is removed. When it closes the caption dissolves and the Firstmate's own note is the first card ever - no host card, no tour, no coach marks - and the input reads "give Firstmate a task, or press/hold right ⌥ to talk" until the captain's first turn. That first turn carries one label on the stage (captain's call 2026-09-30, from the reviewed prototype): "Thinking…" in secondary body text (`--fg-2`, `--text-base`) just above the character, 10 px above the structure's outline, appearing 300 ms after the send once the Firstmate's turn has really started, held at least 900 ms, fading in over `--dur-med` with a 4 px rise and out over `--dur-slow` as the turn ends (opacity alone under reduced motion, where the character itself stands still) - and never again. It says only that work is under way: no progress, no time left, nothing to dismiss, and it is separate from the gate, the welcome note and project setup (the app's `docs/first-launch.md`). Nothing in the first launch surfaces personalize.
- **Firstmate** — the character. A 4D wireframe structure (tesseract projection) of lines and dots with a pair of soft-light eyes in the inner cell (blinking, gaze wandering when idle), continuously animating under an explicit state machine (captain-approved spec: `firstmate/data/fm3000-character-animation-prototypes-s1/report.md`; the app's `src/renderer/src/character/` is the reference implementation — this package's `components/mate/Firstmate.jsx` mock predates the eyes and emotes). Base states: idle = near-still drift (ice cyan) with occasional fidgets; listening = the tesseract shapeshifts flat into two counter-rotating hexagons (Interstellar-robot style) breathing with the voice, spun faster by keystrokes — typing holds listening exactly like voice; working = fast double rotation, shimmer, pulsing nodes. The ember (`--wire-hot`) rides a separate busy parameter, not the state — hot means the agent's own turn is running, even mid-listening, and it cools in place when the turn ends. Consulting is the second parameter over working, never a state: while the agent's turn asks a stronger model the tesseract folds into the crystal - the listening hexagons stood up as a slowly turning hexagonal bipyramid in cool-white light, a band of light climbing its edges every 3s, the ember banked to half in the eyes and cores - and one band comes back down as it unfolds on the answer; attention and emotes still win, and the word "consult" reaches no user surface (the canvas keeps the state name). One-shot emotes overlay the base states and return home on their own: greet (bow + wink on app open), celebrate (spin burst + sparks, on a landed task), ponder, confused (stutter + jitter, on a failed turn), and a fidget pool drawn at random, also on a tap: roll, yawn, orbit, five sky fidgets (the captain's picks, 2026-09-29: Orion and the Big Dipper as traced stick figures on catalog star positions, Saturn with the listening hexagons as its rings and the eyes in the globe, a face-on spiral galaxy with the eyes in the bulge, and Algol with the eyes as the eclipsing pair and the whole light dipping at each eclipse) and the pretend black hole - every one of them in the character's own light, the wires fading as the 16 vertices settle on the figure and returning as it comes home. Five reply emotes answer the replies that carry no card (captain's board verdict, 2026-09-22), each short (1.4-2s) and built from the same parts - a pose, a look, line-art in the character's own light: nod "got it" (two nods, eyes squeezed into happy arcs), salute "on it" (a wind-up, then a snapped quarter turn with two motion arcs), tick "all set" (a light leaves the inner cell and draws a check beside the structure), tuck "noted" (a small light swoops into the inner cell behind a closing ring and one slow blink), aww "any time" (bashful happy eyes glancing away, a shy sway, line-art blush). A reply asked for during the agent's own turn plays as that turn ends, while the ember cools, and the app itself nods for a captain's steer, tucks for a kept note and ticks for an applied personalize. Separate from the emotes, a notice pulse marks a card landing on the stack unseen: one soft ring of light swells out of the structure while the ambient glow lifts, then fades over ~1.4s - it changes no state, cuts nothing short, and reads through the acrylic while the character sits behind the cards. A token flicker marks each finished model request on the character that made it (captain's board verdict, 2026-09-23): the wires flicker like a dim bulb's filament - each edge wavering white-hot on its own phase in four damped pulses over 2s - while the halo takes only a whisper (12%) of it, brightness on a log scale of the request's total tokens (100 tokens barely stirs, 500k and up runs the wires white). No token count ever shows, it changes no state, the resting character is untouched, and under reduced motion it does not play. Transitions are continuous morphs with named clips. Big and central in null state; stays in place behind the cards (dimmed, faintly blurred) while they show, so finishing the stack reveals him again. Voice activation is keybind-only — a plain click on the input focuses it for typing.
- **Cards, not chat** - agent responses arrive as a prioritized stack of cards, one shown at a time. ONE card shape: its chip is derived from what it is, never declared - a card with actions is a decision, one without a note, one the app itself raised (sign in, Firstmate down, a crewmate stuck past every nudge) an attention; a working preview is a decision whose body is interactive (`components/cards/ResponseCard`). No message bubbles ever. A new card never takes the shown card's place, and it is never gone unseen: it lands on the stack unread, the pager marks it (an accent dot on the arrow that leads to it, one "1 new" badge beside the pager - `components/cards/CardStack`) until it is paged to, and the Firstmate gives one notice pulse. A note the captain has already seen steps aside on its own once it is old: it collapses out of the stack into its task record.
- **Tasks** — every ask the captain makes lands in a task record (`FM3K-12` keys, one project per managed repo plus Scratch). The captain reads the record in two places and writes it in none: the **now panel** (right side rail; `components/now/NowPanel`) is what IS - the host title row carries the `filter` control between the panel title and collapse button; expanded content has rows for "waiting on you" and "underway", and "charted" / "landed · 7d" collapsed to a count, with no waiting/underway counts line. Collapsed Tasks retains its compact waiting/underway counts. Everything richer hides behind a click. Clicking a row opens the task's **record card** (`ResponseCard` kind `record`, body `components/cards/TaskRecord`): goal, the captain's words verbatim, graph, latest report, timeline tail, delivery. Its buttons are lifecycle toggles only - Drop task on never-started work, then Start, Stop it, Continue, read off the task's state - and merge, discard and keep stay on cards (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28; Drop task, FI3-243). Every other write, from a steer to a merge, happens by talking to Firstmate; an open record card is what points the turn at that task. A model named in a container's top row is always the model chip (`components/core/Badge`), never truncated and never pushed out of view.
- **Crewmates** — background workers Firstmate delegates to. Rendered as 3D wireframe **solids**, deliberately simpler than the 4D Firstmate (dimensional hierarchy = org hierarchy), and richer for a stronger model: the slot a crewmate is served on picks a **tetrahedron** (low, and any crewmate whose slot is unknown), **octahedron** (medium), **icosahedron** (high) or **geodesic sphere** (premium) - never a hue, label or size (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`). Never a focal point: on the home view each live crewmate orbits the Firstmate on a slowly turning inclined ring up to six crew, then on three differently inclined planes, filling inner to six before middle to six, then outer (overflow spread after all three fill), with older crew gliding inward to fill vacated inner slots, and the captain-approved speeds and directions (`docs/crew-orbits.md`; presence, no labels), crewmates with host-evidenced continuing work heated toward ember and idle ones a dim ice cyan (including cool paused/unknown postures with an honest reason on the Tasks dot; `docs/crew-orbits.md` owns the shared work posture) (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`); the only count is a small overview strip (n working / n idle). Above the strip, an **ActivityFeed** thread logs major crewmate events (spawn / report / decommission) — one-line rows with a colored type dot at the far left and a mono timestamp at the right, chromeless 1px rail, newest at the bottom, a thin left-edge thumb on the rail and a top dissolve when history outgrows the column. Both live in the left side rail as host-framed panels (the feed docks to the bottom, hugs its content, and caps its body at 320px; a feed row wraps to at most two lines at the rail's width); with nothing to show they are absent, and so is the rail.
- **Side rails** - two dock columns, left and right, framing the stage (character, cards, input) on the home view. Empty by default and invisible when empty: zero width, no border, no header, no affordance, so a window with nothing docked is pixel-identical to one without rails. A rail is a vertical stack of host-framed panels at one fixed width (`--rail-width`, never resizable); the host owns each panel's title, attribution, and collapse, and a panel styles only its body region. The stage insets and is never covered. Rails carry contributed UX (the plugin system's `side-panel` slot); the app's own feed is the one panel on the left, and the now panel the one on the right. A panel declares its size: `content` hugs what it shows, `fill` takes the rail height its siblings leave. The app never attributes its own panels; a third party's panel carries its name in the header.
- **Subscriptions** - users add AI subscriptions (Claude, Codex, Grok) and an OpenRouter API key. The app discovers each subscription's models; you place them in four slots - premium, high, medium, low - and a starter placement is filled in when a subscription connects; it routes tasks by slot and remaining quota. Users can override model choice.
- **Where your projects live** - an optional section at the top of Settings -> Projects (`components/projects/ForgeRow`): the app's own sign-in to the place projects live (GitHub for now), a chip row and a device-code aside like the subscriptions', one quiet line when nothing is signed in. A project kept on this Mac never needs it, and nothing anywhere suggests it does.
- **Machines** — SSH hosts the user pools; the app tracks specs and utilization and places tasks.

## Sources
- Quota-tracking domain model: https://github.com/kunchenguid/quota-axi (src/types.ts, src/pace.ts) — provider ids, quota windows, pace/runway/burn-multiple semantics, intelligence buckets.
- No Figma, codebase, or brand assets were provided. **There is no logo**: render "Firstmate 3000" in plain type (Space Grotesk 500) wherever a mark would go. All visuals here are original.

## CONTENT FUNDAMENTALS
- **Tone:** calm, competent, low-ceremony. The app talks like a trusted first officer: brief status, clear options, no exclamation points, no cheerleading.
- **Casing:** sentence case everywhere, including buttons ("Add subscription", "Submit"). Micro-labels are uppercase with wide tracking (`CREW`, `QUOTA`, `ON PACE`).
- **Person:** the app addresses the user as "you"; Firstmate refers to itself sparingly and never says "I'm excited". Task copy is factual: "Refactor finished. 14 files changed."
- **Vocabulary:** every word the app shows is written for someone who has never opened a terminal (`copy/Vocabulary.prompt.md`, the plain-language pass): the say / never-say table is the one home - your project, a pull request, the checks, a branch, a working copy for the isolated copy, merge, a commit, lint, your plan's allowance, your sign-in - and a technical name is allowed only where the person chose it, where it is the thing itself on screen in mono, or one click deeper. The same rule and table reach the models through `CARD_AUTHORING` and the persona prompts. Measured by a hand-scored sample in the replay gate, never a banned-word list.
- **Numbers & data** are always mono (JetBrains Mono): quotas, percentages, host specs, keybinds.
- **Emoji:** never.
- **Examples:** placeholder — "press/hold right ⌥ to talk"; decision card title — "Two ways to fix the flaky test"; crew strip — "3 working · 5 idle"; quota — "62% left · on pace · resets Fri".
- **Card bodies:** semantic HTML in a sandboxed iframe, never one unstructured paragraph. The text the models read is `CARD_AUTHORING` (`src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts`, orchestrator contract v3.6 - the authoring half every persona includes once; the call mechanics live beside it in `CARD_MECHANICS`); this bullet is the design side of the same rule and must not drift from it. A card leads with its answer in one sentence (finished code-work completion cards are the exception: the title alone carries the answer, and the body opens at Why, then What changed, Before and After; `docs/card-authoring.md` owns that loose outline). An answer that explains how something works, compares options, or shows state, shape or layout is drawn - that sentence, then the figure or figures carrying it: inline SVG figures, small tables, a picture a crewmate names from its working copy, or (from a crewmate) an interactive prototype. This is a fact about the card, not a judgment the author makes: the audit `fm3000-card-visual-density-audit-s1` found the old conditional wording obeyed 0 times in 11 by the model family most work routes to, while every concrete rule in the same document was obeyed at or near 100%. An explanation with several parts gets several figures, each beside the short sentence it illustrates, rather than one crowded drawing. Prose carries what a picture cannot - a name, a number, a quote, a caveat - and stays in the open beside the figure it qualifies; `<details>` holds only what a reader who digs would want. The host retains kind, title, close, pager, and footer actions. Use design tokens for app UI: body `--text-base` / `--fg-2`; headings `--text-md` or `--text-base` / `--fg-1` / weight 500 (`h4` `--text-base` / `--fg-2`, `h5` `--text-sm`, `h6` the uppercase tracked micro label in `--text-xs` / `--fg-3`); code and `kbd` `--font-mono` / `--text-sm` (`kbd` is the keycap: `--bg-3`, `--line-1` with a 2px bottom edge, `--radius-s`); links `--accent`; `mark` `--fg-1` on `--accent-dim`; `details` a `--line-1` / `--radius-m` panel whose `summary` is `--fg-1` / weight 500 with a `--fg-3` disclosure caret; `figcaption` `--text-sm` / `--fg-3`; a picture (`img`) is a block that never reaches past the body's width, and one that would stand taller than 360 px shrinks to fit 360 px, whole, letterboxed on `--bg-1` - never cropped; several in a `figure.fm-pictures` are a group, lead and strip: the first leads under that rule, the rest are 88 x 60 thumbnails (`--line-1` border, `--radius-s`) cropped to their top, five shown and then a mono `+N` tile on `--bg-1` counting the rest, beside the fifth while the line has room, and the `figcaption` under them is the group's caption. A click on any picture, or on a group's `+N` tile, opens it large in the picture viewer over the window, paging within its group (`components/cards/PictureViewer.prompt.md`). Figures are inline SVG, written by hand, and no shape is prescribed - draw whatever the explanation calls for. All of SVG renders (any shape, path, gradient, filter, marker, wrapped text via `<foreignObject>`). What makes a figure belong to the app is the design system: a `viewBox` 510 units wide with `width="100%"` for a full-width drawing, or a pixel width when the drawing is smaller so the card only shrinks it, `--fg-2` inherited as `currentColor`, color from theme tokens through `style` (`fill:var(--accent)`, `stroke:var(--line-2)`) so it follows light and dark, `--accent` on the single most-current or lit element within each figure - one accent per figure, not one per card - non-accent tokens for everything else it draws, and `--ok` / `--warn` / `--danger` / `--idle` only for real state, in `StatusDot`'s language (`components/viz/Viz.prompt.md`). External resources are forbidden - the frame loads nothing - though an image the body carries itself as a `data:` URI renders, and so does a picture the host verified and serves from its own copy; `data-fm-action` may mirror a declared action, except any action carrying an effect (`settle`, `open`, or the app's own `host` op), which is the footer button's alone. A card carrying a settle effect ends with the host-rendered fact strip (`.fm-facts`, contract v2.7): one labeled single-line cell per fact - project, crewmate model, the task's effective care (Quick, Default or Careful), the pull request by the label the project's host gave it (`#N` on GitHub, the pushed branch on a plain Git host) as a link only where the host has a page, the checks' state, the CI and review round counts against their caps once the host has counted any (contract v3.6), and the review on a reviewed task - labels in the `h6` micro-label style, identifiers in `--font-mono`, the checks, the caps and review carrying a `StatusDot`-language dot; the checks reading's age, the head the checks last failed on, and the review's risk note ride the cells' `title` attributes. A cell never wraps internally: a too-long value truncates with an ellipsis, and only whole cells wrap to the next row. The body never repeats these facts. A decision with several questions asks them in the body as ordinary named form controls presented however reads best - the proposed option checked, `required` on a must-pick, a bound `<label>` per option - and a pick sends nothing: the footer counts the picks and its button sends them all (`components/cards/ResponseCard.prompt.md`). An inline `<script>` (never `src`) may add behavior - draw a `<canvas>` in token colors read from the frame's computed style, toggle a view, raise a declared action with `fm.action` - and can load nothing. A card whose script stops answering is replaced by one quiet line in the body (`--fg-3`, `--text-sm`: "This card stopped responding.") with a secondary small "Retry" Button beside it; the card chrome stays.

## VISUAL FOUNDATIONS
- **Palette:** deep-space blue-black base (`--bg-0 #05070d`), ice-cyan accent (`--accent #7fdcff`) = the Firstmate's light. Exactly two chromatic families: ice cyan for everything calm (accent, ok, medium bucket) and ember/lava (`--hot #ffa257`, `--danger #ff6b52`) for the occasional hot thing — energy, sun, fire: warnings, high-intelligence bucket, the working Firstmate. Everything else is neutral gray. Light theme via `[data-theme="light"]`. One accent at a time within each thing being read - a screen's chrome, and inside a card each figure on its own, so a card with several figures may light one element per figure; large areas are the tint over the desktop - `--material-tint`, the void at 20% by default - and read against the blurred desktop rather than as a fixed opaque color.
- **Type:** Space Grotesk (UI/display, weights 300–600); JetBrains Mono (data). Display is light (300–400) and large with tight tracking; labels are 11px uppercase tracked +0.09em.
- **Spacing:** 4px scale, generous by default (`--space-5..8` between regions). Emptiness is a feature — the null state is ~90% empty.
- **Backgrounds:** the window is translucent on macOS (the app's `docs/translucent-window.md`): native under-window material on shown Macs, tinted once by the body with `--material-tint` at the chosen wash opacity (20% by default); the app paints no other window-sized surface, no imagery, no gradients except a barely-there radial glow behind Firstmate (`--accent-glow` at low opacity, lifted by `--halo-boost`). No textures, no patterns. Panels stay chromeless on the tint and the voice input's shell is its hairline alone; the card keeps its acrylic and is the only blur the app draws itself. Hairlines (`--line-1`) and tertiary text (`--fg-3`) are set for the material, not the opaque void. Reduce transparency in macOS accessibility brings the opaque `--bg-0` back.
- **Borders & cards:** 1px hairlines `--line-1`. Response cards are **frosted acrylic**: `--acrylic-bg` (6% white) + `backdrop-filter: var(--acrylic-blur)` (20px), `--acrylic-border` hairline, `--acrylic-shadow` (top inner highlight + soft drop). The blurred Firstmate glows through faintly. Opaque `--surface-card` remains for settings rows/non-floating panels. No colored left-border accents.
- **Radii:** 6 / 10 / 16 / pill. The voice input is a pill at one line; taller, it keeps `--prompt-radius` (half its one-line height), never a larger one.
- **Shadows/glow:** shadows are for depth only (dark, diffuse). Glow (`--glow-accent`) is reserved for the Firstmate and active states.
- **Motion:** slow and drifting — `--ease-drift`, 360–700ms. Fades and small translates; never bounces, never spins UI chrome. The only perpetual motion is the Firstmate/crewmate structures.
- **Hover:** background lifts one step (`--bg-3`) or opacity 0.8→1; text stays put. **Press:** no shrink; background darkens slightly. **Focus:** `--focus-ring` (hairline + soft glow), never a browser-default outline.
- **Transparency/blur:** overlays use `--blur-overlay` over `--bg-0` at ~80% opacity — used only for modal-level surfaces.
- **Data viz:** thin 2–3px bars, mono numerals, semantic pace colors; no chart junk.

### Long developer lists

Observe keeps its existing two-pane layout and token styling. Long transcripts and crew lists mount only the viewport plus a small overscan, with measured variable-height rows rather than clipped text or fixed-height guesses. Scrollers persist across updates. Reading history stays anchored to the same row when data or width changes; streaming follows the bottom only while the reader is there. Main, Crew, Review, and Panels keep their worded group headings. The retired supervision session is not a group. Windowing adds no animation or new chrome, and keyboard selection must still reach offscreen sessions.

## ICONOGRAPHY
- **Icon set:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) via CDN (`lucide` UMD), stroke 1.5, sized 14–18px, colored `currentColor`. Chosen for its thin, even stroke that matches the wireframe character. Used sparingly: controls on the voice input (x / check / arrow-up), card actions, settings rows.
- No icon font, no emoji, no unicode-as-icon (except keybind glyphs ⌥ ⌘ ⇧ in KeyCap, which are legitimate keyboard symbols).
- **App icon:** `assets/app-icon.svg` — two nested hexagon rings (outer bright accent, inner twisted 30°, dim) with a center dot: the Firstmate's listening form, calm and geometric. Square 1024 base; masks to macOS squircle / iOS rounded rect (radius ≈ 22.5%). No logo was provided; this mark derives from the character itself.
- The Firstmate and crewmate structures are canvas-rendered, never SVG icons.
- **No logo exists** (none provided; none invented). Wordmark = "Firstmate 3000" in Space Grotesk 500.

## Index
- `styles.css` → `tokens/` (colors, typography, spacing, effects, fonts)

7:- **The first launch** (captain decisions 2026-09-19; the app's `docs/first-launch.md`) — while no subscription can serve Firstmate, the null state carries one caption under the character in the reserved null-state display type, "Connect a subscription to begin", one sentence naming the providers that can serve Firstmate itself (Codex, Grok, Claude, or OpenRouter with an API key), and the provider chip row (`components/core/ConnectChips`) so the sign-in happens right there; the input is `disabled` and dimmed with the line "connect a subscription first", and voice-key presses are ignored. It is state, not a flag: it returns if the last such subscription is removed. When it closes the caption dissolves and the Firstmate's own note is the first card ever - no host card, no tour, no coach marks - and the input reads "give Firstmate a task, or press/hold right ⌥ to talk" until the captain's first turn. That first turn carries one label on the stage (captain's call 2026-09-30, from the reviewed prototype): "Thinking…" in secondary body text (`--fg-2`, `--text-base`) just above the character, 10 px above the structure's outline, appearing 300 ms after the send once the Firstmate's turn has really started, held at least 900 ms, fading in over `--dur-med` with a 4 px rise and out over `--dur-slow` as the turn ends (opacity alone under reduced motion, where the character itself stands still) - and never again. It says only that work is under way: no progress, no time left, nothing to dismiss, and it is separate from the gate, the welcome note and project setup (the app's `docs/first-launch.md`). Nothing in the first launch surfaces personalize.
8:- **Firstmate** — the character. A 4D wireframe structure (tesseract projection) of lines and dots with a pair of soft-light eyes in the inner cell (blinking, gaze wandering when idle), continuously animating under an explicit state machine (captain-approved spec: `firstmate/data/fm3000-character-animation-prototypes-s1/report.md`; the app's `src/renderer/src/character/` is the reference implementation — this package's `components/mate/Firstmate.jsx` mock predates the eyes and emotes). Base states: idle = near-still drift (ice cyan) with occasional fidgets; listening = the tesseract shapeshifts flat into two counter-rotating hexagons (Interstellar-robot style) breathing with the voice, spun faster by keystrokes — typing holds listening exactly like voice; working = fast double rotation, shimmer, pulsing nodes. The ember (`--wire-hot`) rides a separate busy parameter, not the state — hot means the agent's own turn is running, even mid-listening, and it cools in place when the turn ends. Consulting is the second parameter over working, never a state: while the agent's turn asks a stronger model the tesseract folds into the crystal - the listening hexagons stood up as a slowly turning hexagonal bipyramid in cool-white light, a band of light climbing its edges every 3s, the ember banked to half in the eyes and cores - and one band comes back down as it unfolds on the answer; attention and emotes still win, and the word "consult" reaches no user surface (the canvas keeps the state name). One-shot emotes overlay the base states and return home on their own: greet (bow + wink on app open), celebrate (spin burst + sparks, on a landed task), ponder, confused (stutter + jitter, on a failed turn), and a fidget pool drawn at random, also on a tap: roll, yawn, orbit, five sky fidgets (the captain's picks, 2026-09-29: Orion and the Big Dipper as traced stick figures on catalog star positions, Saturn with the listening hexagons as its rings and the eyes in the globe, a face-on spiral galaxy with the eyes in the bulge, and Algol with the eyes as the eclipsing pair and the whole light dipping at each eclipse) and the pretend black hole - every one of them in the character's own light, the wires fading as the 16 vertices settle on the figure and returning as it comes home. Five reply emotes answer the replies that carry no card (captain's board verdict, 2026-09-22), each short (1.4-2s) and built from the same parts - a pose, a look, line-art in the character's own light: nod "got it" (two nods, eyes squeezed into happy arcs), salute "on it" (a wind-up, then a snapped quarter turn with two motion arcs), tick "all set" (a light leaves the inner cell and draws a check beside the structure), tuck "noted" (a small light swoops into the inner cell behind a closing ring and one slow blink), aww "any time" (bashful happy eyes glancing away, a shy sway, line-art blush). A reply asked for during the agent's own turn plays as that turn ends, while the ember cools, and the app itself nods for a captain's steer, tucks for a kept note and ticks for an applied personalize. Separate from the emotes, a notice pulse marks a card landing on the stack unseen: one soft ring of light swells out of the structure while the ambient glow lifts, then fades over ~1.4s - it changes no state, cuts nothing short, and reads through the acrylic while the character sits behind the cards. A token flicker marks each finished model request on the character that made it (captain's board verdict, 2026-09-23): the wires flicker like a dim bulb's filament - each edge wavering white-hot on its own phase in four damped pulses over 2s - while the halo takes only a whisper (12%) of it, brightness on a log scale of the request's total tokens (100 tokens barely stirs, 500k and up runs the wires white). No token count ever shows, it changes no state, the resting character is untouched, and under reduced motion it does not play. Transitions are continuous morphs with named clips. Big and central in null state; stays in place behind the cards (dimmed, faintly blurred) while they show, so finishing the stack reveals him again. Voice activation is keybind-only — a plain click on the input focuses it for typing.
11:- **Crewmates** — background workers Firstmate delegates to. Rendered as 3D wireframe **solids**, deliberately simpler than the 4D Firstmate (dimensional hierarchy = org hierarchy), and richer for a stronger model: the slot a crewmate is served on picks a **tetrahedron** (low, and any crewmate whose slot is unknown), **octahedron** (medium), **icosahedron** (high) or **geodesic sphere** (premium) - never a hue, label or size (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`). Never a focal point: on the home view each live crewmate orbits the Firstmate on a slowly turning inclined ring up to six crew, then on three differently inclined planes, filling inner to six before middle to six, then outer (overflow spread after all three fill), with older crew gliding inward to fill vacated inner slots, and the captain-approved speeds and directions (`docs/crew-orbits.md`; presence, no labels), crewmates with host-evidenced continuing work heated toward ember and idle ones a dim ice cyan (including cool paused/unknown postures with an honest reason on the Tasks dot; `docs/crew-orbits.md` owns the shared work posture) (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`); the only count is a small overview strip (n working / n idle). Above the strip, an **ActivityFeed** thread logs major crewmate events (spawn / report / decommission) — one-line rows with a colored type dot at the far left and a mono timestamp at the right, chromeless 1px rail, newest at the bottom, a thin left-edge thumb on the rail and a top dissolve when history outgrows the column. Both live in the left side rail as host-framed panels (the feed docks to the bottom, hugs its content, and caps its body at 320px; a feed row wraps to at most two lines at the rail's width); with nothing to show they are absent, and so is the rail.
12:- **Side rails** - two dock columns, left and right, framing the stage (character, cards, input) on the home view. Empty by default and invisible when empty: zero width, no border, no header, no affordance, so a window with nothing docked is pixel-identical to one without rails. A rail is a vertical stack of host-framed panels at one fixed width (`--rail-width`, never resizable); the host owns each panel's title, attribution, and collapse, and a panel styles only its body region. The stage insets and is never covered. Rails carry contributed UX (the plugin system's `side-panel` slot); the app's own feed is the one panel on the left, and the now panel the one on the right. A panel declares its size: `content` hugs what it shows, `fill` takes the rail height its siblings leave. The app never attributes its own panels; a third party's panel carries its name in the header.
29:- **Card bodies:** semantic HTML in a sandboxed iframe, never one unstructured paragraph. The text the models read is `CARD_AUTHORING` (`src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts`, orchestrator contract v3.6 - the authoring half every persona includes once; the call mechanics live beside it in `CARD_MECHANICS`); this bullet is the design side of the same rule and must not drift from it. A card leads with its answer in one sentence (finished code-work completion cards are the exception: the title alone carries the answer, and the body opens at Why, then What changed, Before and After; `docs/card-authoring.md` owns that loose outline). An answer that explains how something works, compares options, or shows state, shape or layout is drawn - that sentence, then the figure or figures carrying it: inline SVG figures, small tables, a picture a crewmate names from its working copy, or (from a crewmate) an interactive prototype. This is a fact about the card, not a judgment the author makes: the audit `fm3000-card-visual-density-audit-s1` found the old conditional wording obeyed 0 times in 11 by the model family most work routes to, while every concrete rule in the same document was obeyed at or near 100%. An explanation with several parts gets several figures, each beside the short sentence it illustrates, rather than one crowded drawing. Prose carries what a picture cannot - a name, a number, a quote, a caveat - and stays in the open beside the figure it qualifies; `<details>` holds only what a reader who digs would want. The host retains kind, title, close, pager, and footer actions. Use design tokens for app UI: body `--text-base` / `--fg-2`; headings `--text-md` or `--text-base` / `--fg-1` / weight 500 (`h4` `--text-base` / `--fg-2`, `h5` `--text-sm`, `h6` the uppercase tracked micro label in `--text-xs` / `--fg-3`); code and `kbd` `--font-mono` / `--text-sm` (`kbd` is the keycap: `--bg-3`, `--line-1` with a 2px bottom edge, `--radius-s`); links `--accent`; `mark` `--fg-1` on `--accent-dim`; `details` a `--line-1` / `--radius-m` panel whose `summary` is `--fg-1` / weight 500 with a `--fg-3` disclosure caret; `figcaption` `--text-sm` / `--fg-3`; a picture (`img`) is a block that never reaches past the body's width, and one that would stand taller than 360 px shrinks to fit 360 px, whole, letterboxed on `--bg-1` - never cropped; several in a `figure.fm-pictures` are a group, lead and strip: the first leads under that rule, the rest are 88 x 60 thumbnails (`--line-1` border, `--radius-s`) cropped to their top, five shown and then a mono `+N` tile on `--bg-1` counting the rest, beside the fifth while the line has room, and the `figcaption` under them is the group's caption. A click on any picture, or on a group's `+N` tile, opens it large in the picture viewer over the window, paging within its group (`components/cards/PictureViewer.prompt.md`). Figures are inline SVG, written by hand, and no shape is prescribed - draw whatever the explanation calls for. All of SVG renders (any shape, path, gradient, filter, marker, wrapped text via `<foreignObject>`). What makes a figure belong to the app is the design system: a `viewBox` 510 units wide with `width="100%"` for a full-width drawing, or a pixel width when the drawing is smaller so the card only shrinks it, `--fg-2` inherited as `currentColor`, color from theme tokens through `style` (`fill:var(--accent)`, `stroke:var(--line-2)`) so it follows light and dark, `--accent` on the single most-current or lit element within each figure - one accent per figure, not one per card - non-accent tokens for everything else it draws, and `--ok` / `--warn` / `--danger` / `--idle` only for real state, in `StatusDot`'s language (`components/viz/Viz.prompt.md`). External resources are forbidden - the frame loads nothing - though an image the body carries itself as a `data:` URI renders, and so does a picture the host verified and serves from its own copy; `data-fm-action` may mirror a declared action, except any action carrying an effect (`settle`, `open`, or the app's own `host` op), which is the footer button's alone. A card carrying a settle effect ends with the host-rendered fact strip (`.fm-facts`, contract v2.7): one labeled single-line cell per fact - project, crewmate model, the task's effective care (Quick, Default or Careful), the pull request by the label the project's host gave it (`#N` on GitHub, the pushed branch on a plain Git host) as a link only where the host has a page, the checks' state, the CI and review round counts against their caps once the host has counted any (contract v3.6), and the review on a reviewed task - labels in the `h6` micro-label style, identifiers in `--font-mono`, the checks, the caps and review carrying a `StatusDot`-language dot; the checks reading's age, the head the checks last failed on, and the review's risk note ride the cells' `title` attributes. A cell never wraps internally: a too-long value truncates with an ellipsis, and only whole cells wrap to the next row. The body never repeats these facts. A decision with several questions asks them in the body as ordinary named form controls presented however reads best - the proposed option checked, `required` on a must-pick, a bound `<label>` per option - and a pick sends nothing: the footer counts the picks and its button sends them all (`components/cards/ResponseCard.prompt.md`). An inline `<script>` (never `src`) may add behavior - draw a `<canvas>` in token colors read from the frame's computed style, toggle a view, raise a declared action with `fm.action` - and can load nothing. A card whose script stops answering is replaced by one quiet line in the body (`--fg-3`, `--text-sm`: "This card stopped responding.") with a secondary small "Retry" Button beside it; the card chrome stays.
32:- **Palette:** deep-space blue-black base (`--bg-0 #05070d`), ice-cyan accent (`--accent #7fdcff`) = the Firstmate's light. Exactly two chromatic families: ice cyan for everything calm (accent, ok, medium bucket) and ember/lava (`--hot #ffa257`, `--danger #ff6b52`) for the occasional hot thing — energy, sun, fire: warnings, high-intelligence bucket, the working Firstmate. Everything else is neutral gray. Light theme via `[data-theme="light"]`. One accent at a time within each thing being read - a screen's chrome, and inside a card each figure on its own, so a card with several figures may light one element per figure; large areas are the tint over the desktop - `--material-tint`, the void at 20% by default - and read against the blurred desktop rather than as a fixed opaque color.
35:- **Backgrounds:** the window is translucent on macOS (the app's `docs/translucent-window.md`): native under-window material on shown Macs, tinted once by the body with `--material-tint` at the chosen wash opacity (20% by default); the app paints no other window-sized surface, no imagery, no gradients except a barely-there radial glow behind Firstmate (`--accent-glow` at low opacity, lifted by `--halo-boost`). No textures, no patterns. Panels stay chromeless on the tint and the voice input's shell is its hairline alone; the card keeps its acrylic and is the only blur the app draws itself. Hairlines (`--line-1`) and tertiary text (`--fg-3`) are set for the material, not the opaque void. Reduce transparency in macOS accessibility brings the opaque `--bg-0` back.
36:- **Borders & cards:** 1px hairlines `--line-1`. Response cards are **frosted acrylic**: `--acrylic-bg` (6% white) + `backdrop-filter: var(--acrylic-blur)` (20px), `--acrylic-border` hairline, `--acrylic-shadow` (top inner highlight + soft drop). The blurred Firstmate glows through faintly. Opaque `--surface-card` remains for settings rows/non-floating panels. No colored left-border accents.
39:- **Motion:** slow and drifting — `--ease-drift`, 360–700ms. Fades and small translates; never bounces, never spins UI chrome. The only perpetual motion is the Firstmate/crewmate structures.
41:- **Transparency/blur:** overlays use `--blur-overlay` over `--bg-0` at ~80% opacity — used only for modal-level surfaces.
46:Observe keeps its existing two-pane layout and token styling. Long transcripts and crew lists mount only the viewport plus a small overscan, with measured variable-height rows rather than clipped text or fixed-height guesses. Scrollers persist across updates. Reading history stays anchored to the same row when data or width changes; streaming follows the bottom only while the reader is there. Main, Crew, Review, and Panels keep their worded group headings. The retired supervision session is not a group. Windowing adds no animation or new chrome, and keyboard selection must still reach offscreen sessions.
49:- **Icon set:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) via CDN (`lucide` UMD), stroke 1.5, sized 14–18px, colored `currentColor`. Chosen for its thin, even stroke that matches the wireframe character. Used sparingly: controls on the voice input (x / check / arrow-up), card actions, settings rows.
51:- **App icon:** `assets/app-icon.svg` — two nested hexagon rings (outer bright accent, inner twisted 30°, dim) with a center dot: the Firstmate's listening form, calm and geometric. Square 1024 base; masks to macOS squircle / iOS rounded rect (radius ≈ 22.5%). No logo was provided; this mark derives from the character itself.

A token flicker marks each finished model request on the character that made it (captain's board verdict, 2026-09-23): the wires flicker like a dim bulb's filament - each edge wavering white-hot on its own phase in four damped pulses over 2s - while the halo takes only a whisper (12%) of it, brightness on a log scale of the request's total tokens (100 tokens barely stirs, 500k and up runs the wires white). No token count ever shows, it changes no state, the resting character is untouched, and under reduced motion it does not play. Transitions are continuous morphs with named clips. Big and central in null state; stays in place behind the cards (dimmed, faintly blurred) while they show, so finishing the stack reveals him again. Voice activation is keybind-only — a plain click on the input focuses it for typing.
11:- **Crewmates** — background workers Firstmate delegates to. Rendered as 3D wireframe **solids**, deliberately simpler than the 4D Firstmate (dimensional hierarchy = org hierarchy), and richer for a stronger model: the slot a crewmate is served on picks a **tetrahedron** (low, and any crewmate whose slot is unknown), **octahedron** (medium), **icosahedron** (high) or **geodesic sphere** (premium) - never a hue, label or size (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`). Never a focal point: on the home view each live crewmate orbits the Firstmate on a slowly turning inclined ring up to six crew, then on three differently inclined planes, filling inner to six before middle to six, then outer (overflow spread after all three fill), with older crew gliding inward to fill vacated inner slots, and the captain-approved speeds and directions (`docs/crew-orbits.md`; presence, no labels), crewmates with host-evidenced continuing work heated toward ember and idle ones a dim ice cyan (including cool paused/unknown postures with an honest reason on the Tasks dot; `docs/crew-orbits.md` owns the shared work posture) (rules in `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`); the only count is a small overview strip (n working / n idle). Above the strip, an **ActivityFeed** thread logs major crewmate events (spawn / report / decommission) — one-line rows with a colored type dot at the far left and a mono timestamp at the right, chromeless 1px rail, newest at the bottom, a thin left-edge thumb on the rail and a top dissolve when history outgrows the column. Both live in the left side rail as host-framed panels (the feed docks to the bottom, hugs its content, and caps its body at 320px; a feed row wraps to at most two lines at the rail's width); with nothing to show they are absent, and so is the rail.
12:- **Side rails** - two dock columns, left and right, framing the stage (character, cards, input) on the home view. Empty by default and invisible when empty: zero width, no border, no header, no affordance, so a window with nothing docked is pixel-identical to one without rails. A rail is a vertical stack of host-framed panels at one fixed width (`--rail-width`, never resizable); the host owns each panel's title, attribution, and collapse, and a panel styles only its body region. The stage insets and is never covered. Rails carry contributed UX (the plugin system's `side-panel` slot); the app's own feed is the one panel on the left, and the now panel the one on the right. A panel declares its size: `content` hugs what it shows, `fill` takes the rail height its siblings leave. The app never attributes its own panels; a third party's panel carries its name in the header.
29:- **Card bodies:** semantic HTML in a sandboxed iframe, never one unstructured paragraph. The text the models read is `CARD_AUTHORING` (`src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts`, orchestrator contract v3.6 - the authoring half every persona includes once; the call mechanics live beside it in `CARD_MECHANICS`); this bullet is the design side of the same rule and must not drift from it. A card leads with its answer in one sentence (finished code-work completion cards are the exception: the title alone carries the answer, and the body opens at Why, then What changed, Before and After; `docs/card-authoring.md` owns that loose outline). An answer that explains how something works, compares options, or shows state, shape or layout is drawn - that sentence, then the figure or figures carrying it: inline SVG figures, small tables, a picture a crewmate names from its working copy, or (from a crewmate) an interactive prototype. This is a fact about the card, not a judgment the author makes: the audit `fm3000-card-visual-density-audit-s1` found the old conditional wording obeyed 0 times in 11 by the model family most work routes to, while every concrete rule in the same document was obeyed at or near 100%. An explanation with several parts gets several figures, each beside the short sentence it illustrates, rather than one crowded drawing. Prose carries what a picture cannot - a name, a number, a quote, a caveat - and stays in the open beside the figure it qualifies; `<details>` holds only what a reader who digs would want. The host retains kind, title, close, pager, and footer actions. Use design tokens for app UI: body `--text-base` / `--fg-2`; headings `--text-md` or `--text-base` / `--fg-1` / weight 500 (`h4` `--text-base` / `--fg-2`, `h5` `--text-sm`, `h6` the uppercase tracked micro label in `--text-xs` / `--fg-3`); code and `kbd` `--font-mono` / `--text-sm` (`kbd` is the keycap: `--bg-3`, `--line-1` with a 2px bottom edge, `--radius-s`); links `--accent`; `mark` `--fg-1` on `--accent-dim`; `details` a `--line-1` / `--radius-m` panel whose `summary` is `--fg-1` / weight 500 with a `--fg-3` disclosure caret; `figcaption` `--text-sm` / `--fg-3`; a picture (`img`) is a block that never reaches past the body's width, and one that would stand taller than 360 px shrinks to fit 360 px, whole, letterboxed on `--bg-1` - never cropped; several in a `figure.fm-pictures` are a group, lead and strip: the first leads under that rule, the rest are 88 x 60 thumbnails (`--line-1` border, `--radius-s`) cropped to their top, five shown and then a mono `+N` tile on `--bg-1` counting the rest, beside the fifth while the line has room, and the `figcaption` under them is the group's caption. A click on any picture, or on a group's `+N` tile, opens it large in the picture viewer over the window, paging within its group (`components/cards/PictureViewer.prompt.md`). Figures are inline SVG, written by hand, and no shape is prescribed - draw whatever the explanation calls for. All of SVG renders (any shape, path, gradient, filter, marker, wrapped text via `<foreignObject>`). What makes a figure belong to the app is the design system: a `viewBox` 510 units wide with `width="100%"` for a full-width drawing, or a pixel width when the drawing is smaller so the card only shrinks it, `--fg-2` inherited as `currentColor`, color from theme tokens through `style` (`fill:var(--accent)`, `stroke:var(--line-2)`) so it follows light and dark, `--accent` on the single most-current or lit element within each figure - one accent per figure, not one per card - non-accent tokens for everything else it draws, and `--ok` / `--warn` / `--danger` / `--idle` only for real state, in `StatusDot`'s language (`components/viz/Viz.prompt.md`). External resources are forbidden - the frame loads nothing - though an image the body carries itself as a `data:` URI renders, and so does a picture the host verified and serves from its own copy; `data-fm-action` may mirror a declared action, except any action carrying an effect (`settle`, `open`, or the app's own `host` op), which is the footer button's alone. A card carrying a settle effect ends with the host-rendered fact strip (`.fm-facts`, contract v2.7): one labeled single-line cell per fact - project, crewmate model, the task's effective care (Quick, Default or Careful), the pull request by the label the project's host gave it (`#N` on GitHub, the pushed branch on a plain Git host) as a link only where the host has a page, the checks' state, the CI and review round counts against their caps once the host has counted any (contract v3.6), and the review on a reviewed task - labels in the `h6` micro-label style, identifiers in `--font-mono`, the checks, the caps and review carrying a `StatusDot`-language dot; the checks reading's age, the head the checks last failed on, and the review's risk note ride the cells' `title` attributes. A cell never wraps internally: a too-long value truncates with an ellipsis, and only whole cells wrap to the next row. The body never repeats these facts. A decision with several questions asks them in the body as ordinary named form controls presented however reads best - the proposed option checked, `required` on a must-pick, a bound `<label>` per option - and a pick sends nothing: the footer counts the picks and its button sends them all (`components/cards/ResponseCard.prompt.md`). An inline `<script>` (never `src`) may add behavior - draw a `<canvas>` in token colors read from the frame's computed style, toggle a view, raise a declared action with `fm.action` - and can load nothing. A card whose script stops answering is replaced by one quiet line in the body (`--fg-3`, `--text-sm`: "This card stopped responding.") with a secondary small "Retry" Button beside it; the card chrome stays.
32:- **Palette:** deep-space blue-black base (`--bg-0 #05070d`), ice-cyan accent (`--accent #7fdcff`) = the Firstmate's light. Exactly two chromatic families: ice cyan for everything calm (accent, ok, medium bucket) and ember/lava (`--hot #ffa257`, `--danger #ff6b52`) for the occasional hot thing — energy, sun, fire: warnings, high-intelligence bucket, the working Firstmate. Everything else is neutral gray. Light theme via `[data-theme="light"]`. One accent at a time within each thing being read - a screen's chrome, and inside a card each figure on its own, so a card with several figures may light one element per figure; large areas are the tint over the desktop - `--material-tint`, the void at 20% by default - and read against the blurred desktop rather than as a fixed opaque color.
35:- **Backgrounds:** the window is translucent on macOS (the app's `docs/translucent-window.md`): native under-window material on shown Macs, tinted once by the body with `--material-tint` at the chosen wash opacity (20% by default); the app paints no other window-sized surface, no imagery, no gradients except a barely-there radial glow behind Firstmate (`--accent-glow` at low opacity, lifted by `--halo-boost`). No textures, no patterns. Panels stay chromeless on the tint and the voice input's shell is its hairline alone; the card keeps its acrylic and is the only blur the app draws itself. Hairlines (`--line-1`) and tertiary text (`--fg-3`) are set for the material, not the opaque void. Reduce transparency in macOS accessibility brings the opaque `--bg-0` back.
36:- **Borders & cards:** 1px hairlines `--line-1`. Response cards are **frosted acrylic**: `--acrylic-bg` (6% white) + `backdrop-filter: var(--acrylic-blur)` (20px), `--acrylic-border` hairline, `--acrylic-shadow` (top inner highlight + soft drop). 41:- **Transparency/blur:** overlays use `--blur-overlay` over `--bg-0` at ~80% opacity — used only for modal-level surfaces.
46:Observe keeps its existing two-pane layout and token styling. Reading history stays anchored to the same row when data or width changes; streaming follows the bottom only while the reader is there.     switch flips between today's centre card and the pane on the same fake
    board, so the comparison is honest; a row waiting on you still brings its
    decision card forward, because the pane replaces the record card only.

content.content:
9:- **Cards, not chat** - agent responses arrive as a prioritized stack of cards, one shown at a time. ONE card shape: its chip is derived from what it is, never declared - a card with actions is a decision, one without a note, one the app itself raised (sign in, Firstmate down, a crewmate stuck past every nudge) an attention; a working preview is a decision whose body is interactive (`components/cards/ResponseCard`). No message bubbles ever. A new card never takes the shown card's place, and it is never gone unseen: it lands on the stack unread, the pager marks it (an accent dot on the arrow that leads to it, one "1 new" badge beside the pager - `components/cards/CardStack`) until it is paged to, and the Firstmate gives one notice pulse. A note the captain has already seen steps aside on its own once it is old: it collapses out of the stack into its task record.
10:- **Tasks** — every ask the captain makes lands in a task record (`FM3K-12` keys, one project per managed repo plus Scratch). The captain reads the record in two places and writes it in none: the **now panel** (right side rail; `components/now/NowPanel`) is what IS - the host title row carries the `filter` control between the panel title and collapse button; expanded content has rows for "waiting on you" and "underway", and "charted" / "landed · 7d" collapsed to a count, with no waiting/underway counts line. Collapsed Tasks retains its compact waiting/underway counts. Everything richer hides behind a click. Clicking a row opens the task's **record card** (`ResponseCard` kind `record`, body `components/cards/TaskRecord`): goal, the captain's words verbatim, graph, latest report, timeline tail, delivery. Its buttons are lifecycle toggles only - Drop task on never-started work, then Start, Stop it, Continue, read off the task's state - and merge, discard and keep stay on cards (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28; Drop task, FI3-243). Every other write, from a steer to a merge, happens by talking to Firstmate; an open record card is what points the turn at that task. A model named in a container's top row is always the model chip (`components/core/Badge`), never truncated and never pushed out of view.
59:- `components/voice/` — VoiceInput (idle ↔ recording states)
60:- `components/cards/` — ResponseCard, CardStack, TaskRecord (the record card's body)
