.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md:1:The now panel: what IS, as the `Now` panel of the right side rail (the activity feed on the left says what happened). When expanded, it has no waiting/underway counts line: the host title row carries a dim `filter` control beside the title and collapse button. The list starts below that row with rows for "waiting on you" and "underway", and two collapsed groups that show only their count until clicked: "charted", "landed · 7d". Empty groups are absent. When collapsed, the host header retains its compact waiting/underway counts.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md:11:A row is a `StatusDot`, the task key in dim mono at the start of the title, the title (one line, ellipsized), and, when space permits, the project name in dim mono at the end (ellipsized; the trailing track is `fit-content(40%)` so short names size to content and long names cap at 40%). Hide the project name and its grid track when the panel content is 320px wide or less, or when exactly one registered, non-archived repo project exists (Scratch and archived projects do not count). Count from the full board, not the visible-task filter. The row keeps the full project name in its accessible label and hover title; a blocked or held row carries exactly one dim word after the title; a child row indents under its parent when both belong to the same group. The task key also stays on hover, search, and the row locator. The dot's color says one thing only - what the crewmate on the task is doing, in the colors the Firstmate character paints by: ember while it works, cyan when it sits idle, lava when it was interrupted, hollow when no crewmate is on the task. Waiting on you is the group's word, never a color. Nothing else in the rail: no chips, meters, models, or ages - everything richer hides behind a click.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md:14:<NowPanel counts={{waiting:1,underway:2}} groups={{
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md:19:}} onOpen={(t)=>openRecord(t.id)}/>
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md:22:Clicking a row is a pointing gesture, never a write: a row waiting on you refreshes its ready decision and brings it to the front of the stack (or opens the record if no eligible choice remains); any other row opens the task's record (`TaskRecord`) as the pane docked beside this panel, anchored to the row and tied to it, and that row reads as selected while it is open (`NowDetailPane` in this folder - the captain's call, 2026-09-15, replacing the record card on the stage). The panel has no buttons that change a task, no drag, no inline editing, no manual create - the record's footer carries the lifecycle toggles (`TaskRecord`), and every other write happens by talking to Firstmate. The filter (a key/title search and project chips) sits behind the `filter` affordance and is the panel's own state. Chips keep the project key as the filter handle; row chrome uses the display name. Group headers are the design system's micro labels; a collapsed group's header carries its mono count (the two open groups are already counted on the header line). Charted also counts crew-filed rows the captain has not opened, as ` · N new` beside the count, and such a row's one dim word is `found on <key>` unless it is blocked or held. A collapsible header ends with the host panel expand chevron: the same 14px down stroke the rail uses to collapse a panel, in `--fg-2`, turned 180° so it points up while the group is collapsed and down while it is open. In the app this is a Tier-2 frame template (`src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/now/`), not this JSX; the look is the same, and with nothing to show there is no panel and no rail.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:1:The task-record detail pane: what one now-panel row IS, opened beside the panel instead of on the stage. The captain's call, 2026-09-15, from the prototype review (`docs/prototypes/now-detail-pane.html`): clicking a row used to put the record on the centre card stack, which read as "a card popped up" - in the middle of the window, over the character, in the same pager as unrelated cards, and far from the row it came from.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:3:The pane docks in the right rail's GUTTER: flush to the rail's left edge, one `--space-3` of air between them, top-anchored to the row that opened it and clamped so it never leaves the window (clear of the 52px top bar above, `--space-4` from the bottom). It is wide - up to 520px, growing with the window, never past the rails it sits between - because the record's prose (a goal, the captain's words verbatim, a report) reads badly in a rail-width column. It is the card material: `--acrylic-bg` with `--acrylic-blur`, `--acrylic-border`, `--radius-l`, `--acrylic-shadow`.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:7:- **The tie.** A 12px hairline in `--accent` at 85% opacity, from the pane's right edge to the rail, meeting a 9px notch rotated 45° - the pane's own material with `--accent-glow` on its two leading edges. The tie points at the row's CENTRE and tracks it as the list scrolls, while the pane itself holds still; a row scrolled out of the panel's own viewport drops the tie rather than dragging the pane along or pointing at nothing.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:10:The chrome is the host's and is exactly the record card's (`../cards/TaskRecord.prompt.md`): the status pill with the Tasks rail's dot (tinted whole only for waiting on you or interrupted / failed), the task key in mono with the assigned model as its chip beside it, the title at `--text-lg`, Hide (the cross dismisses the popover and does not drop the task) - and a footer of **lifecycle toggles only**, read off the task's typed state: Drop task on never-started work, Start, Stop it (asking once, inline) or Continue beside Stop it (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28, and Drop task from FI3-243). Merge, discard and keep stay on cards. A crew filing also shows its reason and the Firstmate's one line in the open while it is charted; afterwards they sit in the record under "Why it was filed". Every other write to a task happens by talking to Firstmate while the pane is open. Hiding the popover takes the prompt's focus back, and Escape hides it before it reaches anything else on screen. Neither writes.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:12:What the pane deliberately does NOT do: it does not enter the card stack, so it never pages with the cards and a decision card can sit on the stage beside it; it does not dim or blur the character, because it never claims the stage; and it does not follow the row's x - the gutter is where it lives whatever the rail's width.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:14:In the app this is `src/renderer/src/cards/NowDetailPane.tsx` with its placement arithmetic in `paneGeometry.ts`; the selection is pushed into the panel's sandboxed frame as view state (`fm.onState`) because the frame paints the row and the shell owns what is open.

.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:1:The task-record detail pane: what one now-panel row IS, opened beside the panel instead of on the stage. The captain's call, 2026-09-15, from the prototype review (`docs/prototypes/now-detail-pane.html`): clicking a row used to put the record on the centre card stack, which read as "a card popped up" - in the middle of the window, over the character, in the same pager as unrelated cards, and far from the row it came from.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:3:The pane docks in the right rail's GUTTER: flush to the rail's left edge, one `--space-3` of air between them, top-anchored to the row that opened it and clamped so it never leaves the window (clear of the 52px top bar above, `--space-4` from the bottom). It is wide - up to 520px, growing with the window, never past the rails it sits between - because the record's prose (a goal, the captain's words verbatim, a report) reads badly in a rail-width column. It is the card material: `--acrylic-bg` with `--acrylic-blur`, `--acrylic-border`, `--radius-l`, `--acrylic-shadow`.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:7:- **The tie.** A 12px hairline in `--accent` at 85% opacity, from the pane's right edge to the rail, meeting a 9px notch rotated 45° - the pane's own material with `--accent-glow` on its two leading edges. The tie points at the row's CENTRE and tracks it as the list scrolls, while the pane itself holds still; a row scrolled out of the panel's own viewport drops the tie rather than dragging the pane along or pointing at nothing.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:10:The chrome is the host's and is exactly the record card's (`../cards/TaskRecord.prompt.md`): the status pill with the Tasks rail's dot (tinted whole only for waiting on you or interrupted / failed), the task key in mono with the assigned model as its chip beside it, the title at `--text-lg`, Hide (the cross dismisses the popover and does not drop the task) - and a footer of **lifecycle toggles only**, read off the task's typed state: Drop task on never-started work, Start, Stop it (asking once, inline) or Continue beside Stop it (the captain's 4A, 2026-09-28, and Drop task from FI3-243). Merge, discard and keep stay on cards. A crew filing also shows its reason and the Firstmate's one line in the open while it is charted; afterwards they sit in the record under "Why it was filed". Every other write to a task happens by talking to Firstmate while the pane is open. Hiding the popover takes the prompt's focus back, and Escape hides it before it reaches anything else on screen. Neither writes.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:12:What the pane deliberately does NOT do: it does not enter the card stack, so it never pages with the cards and a decision card can sit on the stage beside it; it does not dim or blur the character, because it never claims the stage; and it does not follow the row's x - the gutter is where it lives whatever the rail's width.
.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowDetailPane.prompt.md:14:In the app this is `src/renderer/src/cards/NowDetailPane.tsx` with its placement arithmetic in `paneGeometry.ts`; the selection is pushed into the panel's sandboxed frame as view state (`fm.onState`) because the frame paints the row and the shell owns what is open.

input.title: Plan: the task record back on the stack, solid cards, the character hidden under them
input.body:
All three fit in one direction with no core change: the task record returns to the card stack as its front entry, the way it was before the pane, every card surface goes solid by redefining four design tokens, and the character's frame fades out whenever the stack holds anything, while the character's loop, the crew orbit and every agent keep running underneath.

Where the record lives

Today the record is a pane docked in the right rail's gutter, tied to its row, and at every window size it hangs over the input and over any card that is up. The proposal puts it back where it was until 2026-09-15: one entry of the stack, shown the moment a row is clicked, paged with the other cards, closed by Hide or Esc. The row stays selected in the Tasks panel while the record is open.

The stack already knew how to do this: the pre-pane store kept a typed stack entry for the record and the card layer rendered it through the same card component; that code is in history and comes back with the pane's newer chrome and lifecycle footer inside it. Nothing about the record changes on the wire: it is still a view the shell holds, never a card row, never emitted by an agent, never a feed line.

How the stack behaves with a record in it

Opening a record shows it at once at the front; a card that lands while it is shown goes behind it unread, with the pager's dot and count, as today. Show the card in the record's waiting box pages to the decision; Hide or Esc closes the record and the card behind it shows; closing the last entry reveals the character again and gives the input its focus back.

Consequences the captain's direction settles: a decision can no longer sit beside an open record, and a turn's hint is the shown entry alone, the record's task when the record is shown and the card's id when a card is. The one change to what the Firstmate sees is that both hints never ride together, which is the rule that held before the pane.

Solid cards are a token change

Five surfaces wear the acrylic and all five read the same four tokens: the card, the stack's peeks, the card-and-thread pair, the record pane and its notch. Redefining the tokens flips every one at once. The sandboxed body frames need nothing: their document is transparent by design, so the body sits on whatever the card paints, and every box the frame stylesheet draws already uses opaque tokens.

TokenDark todayLight todayProposed, both themes
--acrylic-bg6% white40% whitevar(--bg-2), the raised surface the tokens already reserve for cards
--acrylic-blurblur 20pxblur 24px, saturatenone
--acrylic-border10% white14% navyvar(--line-1), the hairline set for the material
--acrylic-shadowhighlight + drophighlight + dropunchanged

I tried it in the built app: a real decision card with a figure, a table, a keycap, a mark and a details panel in its body, first as today, then with the four tokens overridden and the character's frame faded out, in both themes. The test window paints the opaque void rather than the see-through material, so the difference you see at home, the desktop showing through the frosted card, is exactly what the solid card removes.

Hiding the character is a fade, not a stop

The one frame that holds the character, its crew orbit and the first-turn label already dims and blurs while the stack is non-empty. The proposal fades that frame to nothing over the slow motion token and hides it once the fade ends, and fades it back the same way when the last entry closes; under reduced motion it snaps. The animation loops, the character's state machine, the orbit model, the emote and flicker channels and every agent turn are untouched: only pixels go.

Two things live in that frame today and go with it: the first-turn Thinking… label, and the model labels being built above each crewmate, which must mount inside the same frame so the one switch covers them. Both are fine to lose under a card: a card is a stronger sign of work than either label. One thing loses its surface: the notice pulse that marks a card landing behind the shown one reads through the acrylic today, and with the character gone it has nowhere to show; the pager's dot and its count already say the same thing.

Questions, with the answer I would give

1. Where does an opened record land in the pager?
2. How many records can be open?
3. The pane closes on a click anywhere outside it. As a card?
4. Which surface does a solid card paint?
5. How does the character leave and return?
6. While hidden, do the animation loops keep running?
7. The notice pulse for a card landing behind the shown one loses its surface.
8. The Thinking label and the coming model labels sit in the character's frame.
9. What does Esc do with a record on the stack?

Waiting for the next round: if you pick pause in 6, whether emotes queued while paused play on return or are dropped; if you pick the end in 1, whether the Tasks row stays selected while its record is not the shown entry.

What I assumed

  • The record stays a shell-held view: no card row, no agent can emit one, no feed line, the core's card stack untouched.
  • Its chrome inside the card is the pane's: status pill with the Tasks dot, key, model chip, title, Hide; its footer stays the lifecycle toggles; Show the card keeps pointing at the decision.
  • It is a regular-width card with the edge drag every lone card has, no thread and no reply row; its body scrolls inside the card like any long body.
  • An open record counts as a card for the stage: the character hides and the screen reads Working, which is the ask.
  • The Tasks row stays selected while its record is open; the panel's row-anchor reporting and the pane's placement arithmetic are removed, and the bridge script is untouched.
  • The token change lands in both token homes, the app's and the design skill's, with the skill's readme and the docs that still say acrylic; the picture viewer's overlay keeps its own blur, it is a modal, not a card.
  • No new setting for any of this.

Unchanged contracts, exclusions, and the order to ship

Unchanged: the card wire shape and its refusals, cards as threads and the close-out rule, whose turn and the idle ladder, the Tasks panel's gestures and its selected-row push, the record body template and the tasks.detail read, the lifecycle ops and Drop task, the character machine, the orbit model, the emotes and flicker, the Firstmate's context and hint resolution, the window material and the wash slider. Out of scope: the model labels build itself, any change to the Thinking label's own timing, pausing agent work, the Settings view, which already unmounts the character.

  1. Solid surfaces. Four token values in both homes plus the doc lines that say acrylic, and one end-to-end read that the card surface computes to no blur and an opaque fill in both themes. Small.
  2. Hide the character. The dim and blur on the character's frame become a fade to hidden with a reduced-motion duration token like the stage lift's, plus the design readme line that says dimmed and faintly blurred; the specs that assert the character visible under a card assert it hidden instead. Small.
  3. The record on the stack. The typed stack entry and its index rules return to the store, the card layer renders the record through the card component with the pane's chrome and footer, the pane, its geometry and the panel's anchor reporting go, and the end-to-end journeys that find the pane find the record card through the shared helpers instead. The largest piece, mostly tests and docs.

Each piece merges on its own. Once the pane is gone, the open task about a solid black backdrop behind the popover, FI3-139, is moot.

Frames are transparent at plugins/frames/frameStylesheet.ts:53.
  • The character's frame: HomeScreen.tsx:858-870 (opacity 0.45 and blur 3px while the phase is working, the crew orbit and the first-turn label inside it); loops in character/motion.ts:12, character/Firstmate.tsx:1510, character/crew/CrewOrbit.tsx:79, pausing only on a hidden document; the reduced-motion duration precedent is --stage-lift-duration in design/styles.css.
  • The Firstmate's hint: src/core/orchestrator/firstmateAgent.ts:754-766 takes an explicit task id first, else the shown card's task.
  • The Tasks panel: plugins/builtin/tasks/nowActions.ts (open and point), panel.tsx:213-248 (anchor reporting), plugins/builtin/index.ts (selected row pushed as frame state).
Tests and docs the record move touches

End-to-end specs that find the pane: now-panel.spec.ts (24 references, including the geometry at 294-340 and the Null state reads at 331 and 484, which become Working), record-controls.spec.ts (21), frame-scrollbar-threshold.spec.ts (4), closed-blockers.spec.ts (3), answer-task.spec.ts and card-threads.spec.ts (2 each); all reach it through rails.ts's hideRecord and recordFrame, so the locator moves once there. Unit: paneGeometry.test.ts goes, store.test.ts 401-470 and 852-880, nowActions.test.ts, RecordPaneChrome.test.tsx. For the hide, phase1-shell.spec.ts:115 reads the character during a turn with no card up and keeps passing; a grep for the character's role name finds 27 specs, to be checked one by one for a card-up read.

Docs: the design skill's readme (the character bullet says dimmed and faintly blurred; the backgrounds and borders bullets say acrylic; the Tasks bullet already says record card), components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md, NowDetailPane.prompt.md, components/cards/TaskRecord.prompt.md, ResponseCard.prompt.md, CardStack.prompt.md; docs/translucent-window.md (the card as the app's only blur), docs/ui-plugins.md P4 section, docs/renderer.md record sizing.

How the pictures were taken

A throwaway spec in this working copy, not committed: seed one idle task and one decision card with a rich body into a scratch data folder, launch the built app hidden at 1200 by 800 with the mock provider, screenshot, open the record from the Tasks row with an in-frame click, screenshot, then append a style element setting the four tokens and fade the character's frame to opacity 0, screenshot, switch the theme in Settings, screenshot, remove the overrides, screenshot. The hidden test window paints the opaque void, so no picture shows the desktop through the acrylic.

input.title: Plan: the task record back on the stack, solid cards, the character hidden under them
input.body:
All three fit in one direction with no core change: the task record returns to the card stack as its front entry, the way it was before the pane, every card surface goes solid by redefining four design tokens, and the character's frame fades out whenever the stack holds anything, while the character's loop, the crew orbit and every agent keep running underneath.

Where the record lives

Today the record is a pane docked in the right rail's gutter, tied to its row, and at every window size it hangs over the input and over any card that is up. The proposal puts it back where it was until 2026-09-15: one entry of the stack, shown the moment a row is clicked, paged with the other cards, closed by Hide or Esc. The row stays selected in the Tasks panel while the record is open.

The stack already knew how to do this: the pre-pane store kept a typed stack entry for the record and the card layer rendered it through the same card component; that code is in history and comes back with the pane's newer chrome and lifecycle footer inside it. Nothing about the record changes on the wire: it is still a view the shell holds, never a card row, never emitted by an agent, never a feed line.

How the stack behaves with a record in it

Opening a record shows it at once at the front; a card that lands while it is shown goes behind it unread, with the pager's dot and count, as today. Show the card in the record's waiting box pages to the decision; Hide or Esc closes the record and the card behind it shows; closing the last entry reveals the character again and gives the input its focus back.

Consequences the captain's direction settles: a decision can no longer sit beside an open record, and a turn's hint is the shown entry alone, the record's task when the record is shown and the card's id when a card is. The one change to what the Firstmate sees is that both hints never ride together, which is the rule that held before the pane.

Solid cards are a token change

Five surfaces wear the acrylic and all five read the same four tokens: the card, the stack's peeks, the card-and-thread pair, the record pane and its notch.
